engine-net-core.summary: Сетевое ядро работает, но написано тяжеловесно. Самые дорогие места в сети такие. Каждая рассылка хоста (net::host_broadcast → Mode::deliver) заново копирует список игроков вместе со строками, причём в обоих режимах. Хост в коопе делает такую же копию каждый кадр в host_has_company. Снимки NPC раз в 66 мс собирают по несколько куч-выделений на каждое существо и шлют трупы, которые клиент уже не двигает. Клиент каждый кадр копирует сэмпл каждой марионетки вместе с вектором навесок. Все эти правки не меняют того, что видит игрок: меняются только выделения памяти и лишняя работа. Ошибок в синхронизации я не нашла. Нашла три мелкие: набор «залогировать один раз» в Session никогда не чистится и растёт; Manager::stop() не снимает паузу «хост молчит»; поток загрузки читает m_phase без atomic. Красоты не хватает сильнее всего. coop_requests.cpp (4876 строк) и coop_join.cpp (4549, с одной структурой State на ~100 полей) собирают по 8–10 обязанностей каждый, ниже план разбиения по уже размеченным секциям. Условие «решаю ли я здесь» (decides_world() || leads_level()) скопировано 84 раза. Мелкие помощники (find_go, put_vec, log_allowed, before_live, FNV, pack_unit) живут в 3–12 копиях, иногда с разным поведением. Есть мёртвые функции и обёртки, которые просто возвращают аргумент. В комментариях около 714 строк истории (даты, номера ревью, R/F/W/TZ). Где какой поток работает, файлы описывают по-разному: одни ставят блокировки «на всякий случай», другие те же хуки не защищают вовсе. Начинать советую с API Session, которое отдаёт подключённых игроков без копирования: оно убирает сразу три горячие точки. Затем единый предикат «решаю здесь» и разбиение двух больших файлов. Всё это проверено только чтением, ничего не собирала и не замеряла.

kept.title: Every world broadcast copies the whole peer list (vector<PeerInfo> with strings)
kept.detail: net::host_broadcast (coop_net.cpp:49) -> Mode::deliver. The co-op deliver does `for (const PeerInfo& p : s.peers())` (coop_hostplay_mode.cpp:62), and the server's to_players does the same (srv/coop_srv_mode.cpp:101). Session::peers() (xrCoop/coop_session.cpp:2315-2330) builds a new std::vector and copies each PeerInfo (two std::string: nick and address 'ip:port', which is usually longer than the 15-char SSO, plus a 32-byte key). This runs for every EntitySnapshot packet (several per 66 ms), every objects Batcher flush (coop_objects.cpp:334), every EntityParent/EntityDied/EntityLocal (coop_events.cpp:1095-1119) and so on. Estimate: 100-300 broadcasts/s on a busy host, times 1+2N heap allocations each for N clients. The comment at line 66 ('R1 5: no players() vector per message') removed players() but kept peers().
kept.fix: Add a const view to Session: `template<class F> void for_each_joined(F&&) const` over m_joined, or `const std::vector<PeerId>& joined_ids() const` cached and rebuilt on join/leave. Use it in both deliver/to_players. Keep the same iteration order (std::map by PeerId), so the send order stays the same.
kept.correction: The mechanism is right: Session::peers() (coop_session.cpp:2315-2330) builds a vector and copies each PeerInfo, and it runs for every host_broadcast through hostplay deliver (:62) and srv to_players (:101). EntitySnapshot (coop_entities.cpp:832) and the Batcher (coop_objects.cpp:334) really do use host_broadcast. Payoff 'high' is overstated: a nick of 15 characters or fewer fits SSO, so each broadcast costs 1 + N allocations (the vector plus each 'ip:port' string). That is a few hundred to about a thousand small allocations per second in co-op, roughly 0.1 ms/s, with no visible FPS effect. Payoff: low in co-op, medium on a world server with many players. The fix (a view over m_joined, a std::map, so the order is kept) stands, risk low.

kept.title: coop_requests.cpp (4876 lines) mixes ~10 responsibilities; split along its own section markers
kept.detail: Sections already in the file: hit wire + damage (222-330, 588-662, 3267-3345, 4996-5110); weapon riders (662-730); silencer detach (380-430, 3543-3628); leased ids, client (429-600, 1098-1560) and host (2145-2330); clone/replacement (127-141, 443-475, 3903-4160); refused-upgrade rebuild (973-1098); personal map zones (1750-1868); host request gate (1868-2000); spawn settings/budget (2001-2145) and spawn build/queue (2330-2783); moves/admission/destroy (2783-3267); upgrades at a mechanic (3345-3530); rockets (3729-3880); Lua wrappers (4700-4995). Only the client outbox/inflight (332-972, 4440-4700) and install/reset/frame/print_status (4168-4440) are 'requests' proper.
kept.fix: Move code without changing it into coop_requests_hits.cpp, _leases.cpp, _clone.cpp, _spawn.cpp, _moves.cpp, _item_events.cpp (upgrades + silencer + rebuild), _rockets.cpp, _lua.cpp, plus coop_local_zones.cpp. Shared state (g_out_lock, g_outbox, Action, Inflight) goes into a private coop_requests_impl.h. Keep reset()/frame() as the single list in coop_requests.cpp. Do it as a pure move first, then the dedups below.
kept.correction: The file has 5117 lines, not 4876 (the section line numbers in the finding already reach 5110). The section markers are at 220, 332, 429, 662, 973, 1098, 1750, 1868, 2001, 2145, 2528, 2944, 3345, 3729, 4168, 4440, 4700 and 4996. The split as a pure move stands. Most shared state sits in the anonymous namespace at 79-3901, so the private impl header is needed as proposed.

kept.title: coop_join.cpp (4549 lines) with one god-struct State g (~100 fields of 8 features)
kept.detail: `struct State` (120-291) holds host join, client join, the character choice (protocol 8), the transition board, the simultaneous load and load screen, level moves, seat holds, the guide trip and map saves. The file also contains destroyed-object stack diagnostics (76-100), char-script Lua glue (323-450), proxy creation and key admission (489-1270), world save/send/WorldLoaded (1270-1830), level-changer geometry (1830-2064), simultaneous load (2064-2756), level moves (2756-2875), board/transition_step (2875-3172), the Lua transition API (3172-3324), the client cache (4106-4172), the arrival journal (4537-4606) and the role swap (4606-4786). `g = State()` at 4209 resets all of it at once.
kept.fix: Split into coop_join.cpp (gate, world send, WorldLoaded, watchers, frame), coop_join_characters.cpp (proxy, keys, new and creator character, char Lua), coop_transition.cpp (board, transition_step, Lua transition API, host_gate_level_change, level trip), coop_transition_load.cpp (prepared load, load screen, level moves, seat holds), coop_join_swap.cpp (on_alife_objects_loaded). Move arrival and diag stacks to coop_instrument/coop_debug. Give each file its own sub-state struct and a reset(), called from the one reset list.
kept.correction: The file has 4786 lines, not 4549. struct State spans 120-291 with about 115 declarations, and g = State() is at 3663 (on_host_started) and 4209. The split proposal stands.

kept.title: 'Do I decide here' is spelled `mode().decides_world() || mode().leads_level()` 84 times
kept.detail: Counted with grep over coop/*.cpp: objects 17, items 12, requests 10, events 8, entities 5 (e.g. coop_entities.cpp:2111, 2332, 2687), net 1, plus srv/hostplay. net::host() (coop_net.cpp:12) is the same predicate with active(), and net::host_send (coop_net.cpp:55) repeats it negated. This is exactly the P12 question 'do I decide here', and it has no name.
kept.fix: Add `bool Mode::decides_here() const { return decides_world() || leads_level(); }` in xrCoop/coop_mode.h (or a free coop::decides_here()). Replace all 84 copies mechanically. net::host() becomes `mgr().active() && mode().decides_here()`.

kept.title: Host snapshot (66 ms) allocates several buffers per creature and copies each packet twice
kept.detail: host_send_snapshots (816-876): `Writer entry(128)` is a std::vector reserve, so one heap allocation per creature per tick (849). capture_attachments(obj) (869, 475-499) builds an attachments::State with std::vector<Item{std::string bone}> per creature. It walks attached_objects() with a CTorch dynamic cast, and creature_flags -> attached_torch (508-509) walks the same list again. Then w.bytes(entry) copies the entry, and flush() (829) allocates `Writer out` and copies the whole packet again to prepend the 6-byte header. For 100 creatures at 15 Hz that is about 1500+ allocations/s plus the copies, on the main thread of the decider.
kept.fix: Write entries straight into one persistent packet Writer. Reserve 6 header bytes at clear() and patch time/count at flush, which needs a Writer::patch_u16/u32 or writing at offset. Write attachments directly (count, then items) without building a State. Do one attached_objects() pass that yields both the torch and the list. Keep the produced bytes identical (same order, same budget rule).
kept.correction: Confirmed: `Writer entry(128)` reserves a std::vector, one heap allocation per creature per tick (coop_entities.cpp:849). flush() then allocates `Writer out` and copies the packet again (829-833). The same out-copy pattern exists in objects Batcher::flush (coop_objects.cpp:324-332). Corrections: capture_attachments allocates only for creatures with non-torch attachments (an empty std::vector does not allocate, and short bone names fit SSO). About 1500 allocations/s costs about 0.1-0.2 ms/s, so payoff is low, not medium. The fix needs a new patch/offset write in xrCoop/coop_wire.h Writer (pure C++ that the unit tests use too).

kept.title: Client copies a full MirrorSample (with attachments vector) per puppet per frame
kept.detail: drive_mirror (2613) is called per remote puppet per frame (coop_remote.cpp:310). It calls interpolate(), which does `out = t.samples.front()` / `out = k < 0.5f ? a : b` / `out = t.samples.back()` (2074, 2085, 2092). MirrorSample holds attachments::State (std::vector<Item> with std::string), so a puppet with attachments costs a heap allocation per frame. Then `s.attachments == track.attachments_shown` (2646) deep-compares it every frame. Also client_on_snapshot does `t.samples.push_back(s)` (1858), a copy instead of a move.
kept.fix: Have interpolate fill only pos/yaw/aim/health/anims and return a pointer to the chosen sample (a or b by k, as today). Read flags, held and attachments by const reference from that sample. Use std::move(s) at 1858. Same values are chosen, so nothing visible changes.
kept.correction: Confirmed: interpolate copies a whole MirrorSample (coop_entities.cpp:2074, 2085, 2092), drive_mirror compares attachments every frame (2646), and push_back(s) at 1858 copies (s is not used afterwards). A heap allocation happens only for puppets with non-torch attachments; otherwise it is a memcpy of about 200 bytes. Payoff is low, not medium. Side note: the comment at 2643 says 'flags from the newest sample', but s is a or b by k, not the newest. Fix that comment, or the code, without changing behaviour.

kept.title: Co-op host copies the peer list every frame to ask 'is anybody else here'
kept.detail: join::frame -> transition_step (4439, 3012-3015) -> group_waits_here (1950-1955) -> host_has_company (1937-1946) iterates `mgr().session().peers()`, which is a new vector<PeerInfo> with string copies, every frame on the co-op host. host_board_step adds players() at 10 Hz (2951), and players() calls peers() again (coop_session.cpp:2395).
kept.fix: Use `Session::joined_count()` or the for_each_joined view from finding 1. players() at 2951 can use the same view plus the local-player row.
kept.correction: Confirmed: host_has_company (coop_join.cpp:1937-1946) calls peers() every frame through transition_step, but only on the co-op host and only while it has an actor (group_waits_here 1950-1955). host_board_step (100 ms timer at 2918) calls players() -> peers(). Session has no joined_count(), so it must be added (or use the view from finding 0). The cost is one vector plus N string copies per frame, so payoff is low, not medium.

kept.title: Corpses are streamed in EntitySnapshot at 15 Hz although clients never drive a dead puppet
kept.detail: The snapshot loop filters only !getDestroy, is_creature and !player_proxy (842). There is no life check, so every dead stalker or monster online on the decider gets capture_anims, creature_flags, attachments and ~30-60 bytes per peer every 66 ms. On the client, remote::apply returns false for !g_Alive (coop_remote.cpp:280-283), so drive_mirror (the only consumer of g_tracks besides describe_copy) never runs for them. Ragdoll poses already go through objects::host_stream (classify -> Body for dead creatures, coop_objects.cpp:376-385). GAMMA levels accumulate dozens of corpses.
kept.fix: Skip creatures with !g_Alive() once their death has been relayed for longer than a grace that covers the client's pending-death window (events kPendingTimeoutMs = 15 s, coop_events.cpp:56). For example, keep a death time per id set in events::host_on_death. Measure bytes/s in coop_status before and after.

kept.title: Session's 'log once' set is never cleared: grows for the life of the process and silences later sessions
kept.detail: m_logged_once (274) is filled by first_time() (332) with keys like 'sendfail<serial>' (693), 'stale-in<serial>:<epoch>' (877), 'stale-out<serial>:<epoch>:<epoch>' (1014), 'send-nopeer<id>' (2434), 'virt-nopeer<id>' (382). hard_stop() (1986-2019) does not clear it, and the Session lives as long as the Manager. On a long-running world server it grows with every reconnect and epoch. Per-peer-id keys mean that peer slot 3 never logs that line again in any later session. may_send/game_message also build 3 to_string concatenations plus a set lookup for every message to or from a stale-epoch peer, i.e. every snapshot during a client's reload.
kept.fix: Clear m_logged_once and m_logged_unknown in hard_stop(). Replace the string keys with per-Conn flags (for example `uint32_t stale_out_logged_epoch` and `bool send_fail_logged` in Conn) and a small enum-keyed set for the rest, so no string is built per message.

kept.title: Five hand-maintained lists of 25 modules, and the start and end lists already differ
kept.detail: init (65-74), install_server (76-101), install_client (103-128), on_session_started (130-157), reset (176-209), frame (236-300) and print_status (302-337) each list the modules by hand. on_session_started omits vehicles::session_over, npc_ai::viewers_clear, player_touch::reset, world::reset, net::reset and progress::reset, which reset() has. money and debug use different entry points (on_session_started vs reset). A new module has to be added in 5-7 places in the right order.
kept.fix: Use one constexpr table `struct Module { const char* name; void(*install_server)(Session&); void(*install_client)(Endpoint&); void(*reset)(); void(*frame)(bool up, bool gap); void(*print_status)(); }` in call order, with the frame gate (up/!gap/always) as a field. Write down for each module whether start needs anything beyond reset, and make that a field rather than a second list.

kept.title: Three vocabularies for 'who am I' live side by side (roles, Mode, Phase) with transitional names
kept.detail: coop_manager.h:60-65 says 'Until a module is moved over, the old names keep their meaning': is_host() = role WorldServer, is_client() = WorldClient. Lines 130-137 add is_world_server/is_map_authority/is_player/is_mirror/is_live_mirror ('the old is_live_client()'). Mode adds decides_world/leads_level/actor_is_player, Phase adds is_live_client, and net adds host()/client()/live() (coop_net.cpp:11-13). Modules mix them: events before_live uses mgr().is_live_client() (coop_events.cpp:194), objects uses is_live_mirror() (coop_objects.cpp:226), requests frame uses is_mirror() (4292). docs/MODES.md wants the Core to ask only the mode.
kept.fix: Finish the migration. Keep Mode::decides_here()/leads_level()/where() plus is_live() in Core and delete the 'old names' block and its comment. Convert the call sites module by module, one test pass per module, and add a check_layers rule that bans is_host()/is_client() in new code.
kept.correction: The three vocabularies are confirmed (coop_manager.h:60-65, 130-137; coop_net.cpp:11-13; events:194 is_live_client, objects:226 is_live_mirror, requests:4292 is_mirror). The migration is not mechanically behaviour-neutral. Outside a session, mode() is NoneMode with decides_world=false and leads_level=false (coop_mode.h:307-313), while the roles are 0. Before Welcome, roles_of falls back to client_roles() (coop_manager.cpp:173-180). So, for example, is_client() is not the same as !mode().decides_world() in single player: every conversion must add mgr().active() and keep the pre-Welcome fallback. behaviour_change becomes 'possible per call site'. Risk stays medium, and each module needs its own test pass.

kept.title: Threading rule differs per file for the same engine hooks
kept.detail: coop_manager.h:3 says 'Everything runs on the game main thread'. events locks its hook data while saying 'They never overlap in this engine, the lock only keeps that an assumption' (61-63). entities fills g_host_events from the same ALife/server hooks with no lock ('game thread or main thread, never concurrently with frame()', coop_entities.cpp:91-92), while host_on_entity_released calls syncapi 'any game thread' (2283). items uses std::mutex g_lock (coop_items.cpp:208), objects and requests use xrCriticalSection (coop_objects.cpp:207, coop_requests.cpp:413, 513), and requests takes g_out_lock around g_inflight in one place (781-788) and not in others (758, 815, 847). If a hook ever runs off the main thread, entities' vector races. If none does, about 6 locks are noise.
kept.fix: Decide one rule and enforce it. Recommended: every coop hook is main-thread. Add `VERIFY(is_main_thread())` (Core.main_thread_id or similar) at hook entry points, drop the defensive locks, and fix the comments. If some hook really is off-thread, give it one shared lock type and protect entities' g_host_events too.
kept.correction: The inconsistency is real: events g_lock (coop_events.cpp:61-63), entities g_host_events with no lock (coop_entities.cpp:91), items std::mutex (coop_items.cpp:208), objects and requests xrCriticalSection, and requests calling track() into g_inflight without the lock at 758 but under it at 781-788. The recommended fix is wrong, though. The code itself says hooks run off the main thread: coop_mode.h:16-17 ('the ALife may ask from its own thread'), coop_entities.cpp:91 ('game thread or main thread'), coop_items.cpp:212 ('a Lua create may run on the game thread'), coop_requests.cpp:412 and LocatorAPI.cpp:140 ('the main thread and the game thread of the MT build at the same time'). A VERIFY(is_main_thread()) at the hook entry points would fire. The correct rule to enforce is 'hooks may run on the game thread but never during coop frame()': assert it with an atomic in-frame flag, use one lock type, and guard g_host_events the same way the others are guarded. Do not drop the locks unless the non-overlap is proven.

kept.title: find_go/valid_go copied in 4-5 files
kept.detail: The identical body `net_Find(id)` + `!getDestroy()` appears in coop_events.cpp:153-159, coop_objects.cpp:232-238, coop_requests.cpp:181-187 and coop_vehicles_client.cpp:154-160, plus entities::game_object_here (coop_entities.cpp:103-109) and the inline copy in placement_position (134-138). valid_go (with object_removed) appears in events 162 and requests 189.
kept.fix: Put `CGameObject* live_object(u16 id)` and `CGameObject* server_valid_object(u16 id)` once in a Core header (coop_world.h or a new coop_objects_here.h) and delete the copies.

kept.title: objects defines its own pack_unit/unpack_unit that rounds differently from the shared one
kept.detail: coop_objects.cpp:255-256: `u16 pack_unit(float)` uses iFloor(clampr(f)*32767), i.e. rounds down, and `unpack_unit(u16)` does not clamp. xrCoop/coop_protocol.h:684-694 has `int16_t pack_unit(float)` with round-to-nearest and a clamping unpack, used by entities (coop_entities.cpp:586, 1838). These are two quantizers under the same name for the same wire concept (quaternion components).
kept.fix: Delete the objects copy and use the protocol one, adding a u16 cast at the call sites. The body quaternion encoding moves by at most 1 LSB (1/32767), so it is not visible, but it changes the wire bytes: test with both modes.

kept.title: before_live exists twice with different 'live' tests
kept.detail: coop_events.cpp:192-198 drops world messages unless `mgr().is_live_client()`, while coop_objects.cpp:224-230 uses `is_live_mirror()` (= is_mirror() && is_live_client(), coop_manager.h:134). On a process that is a live client of its world but not a mirror (a map server: Mode::leads_level), the two modules apply opposite rules for the same rules::live_only messages.
kept.fix: Use one helper in coop_net.h (for example `bool drops_before_live(Msg)`). Decide which predicate is meant and write the reason in one comment. If the objects variant is the intended one for map servers, say so there.
kept.correction: The duplicate is real, but the 'opposite rules on a map server' claim is wrong. The two functions guard different message types: objects guards EntityState and ZoneState (coop_objects.cpp:1663, 1762), events guards EntityParent, EntityDied, EntityVisual and EntityLocal (coop_events.cpp:795-909). Both objects callers return on !is_mirror() first (1657-1658, 1759-1760), so at the call sites is_live_mirror() reduces to is_live_client(), the same test events uses. Unify on is_live_client() with no behaviour change. Each module keeps its own dropped_before_live counter, so the shared helper should take the counter or return a bool only. Kind: duplicate/style. Modes: both, not server.

kept.title: Content manifest reads every loose text file of gamedata on the main thread at the first session start
kept.detail: Manager::manifest() (284-328) runs at the first make_config (start_host/start_client). For each loose file it calls manifest_text_file and then FS.r_open/scans the whole file for its LF size (315-320), on the main thread. With GAMMA's thousands of loose .script/.ltx files through MO2 that is a visible hitch when pressing Host/Connect. The duration is logged as '[coop] content manifest: N entries, ..., X ms' (325).
kept.fix: Check X in a stand log first. If it is above about 100 ms, start the manifest on a worker thread at boot (std::async after FS init; it touches only FS read APIs) and wait on the future in make_config. An alternative is to cache (name, size, mtime) -> lf_size in appdata. The result is identical.
kept.correction: Confirmed: Manager::manifest (coop_manager.cpp:284-328) opens and scans every loose text file of gamedata on the main thread at the first make_config, and logs the time at 325. No log with that line was found in the repo, so the cost is still unmeasured. Measure it first, as the finding says. The risk of the std::async variant is medium, not low: FS calls take the process-wide recursive FS_FILES_GUARD (LocatorAPI.cpp:144-149), so a worker doing thousands of r_open calls during boot would stall the main thread's file lookups. Prefer the (name, size, mtime) -> lf_size cache, which is low risk.

kept.title: Two independent full Level().Objects walks every 66 ms on the decider
kept.detail: entities::host_send_snapshots (coop_entities.cpp:839) and objects::host_stream (coop_objects.cpp:2253) each iterate every object of the level (items on the ground included) every 66 ms, with separate timers (g_last_snapshot / g_last_stream). Only creatures, respectively physics shell holders, are wanted. The client also walks everything in objects::client_scan every 500 ms (848), and watch_decider every 10 s (coop_entities.cpp:444).
kept.fix: Keep id registries filled from the existing spawn/destroy hooks (remote::on_net_spawn and on destroy): creatures for snapshots, physics bodies for the stream. Iterate those instead. Keep the per-entry order (or sort by id) so the packet layout stays deterministic.

kept.title: Manager::stop() leaves the 'host silent' pause state set
kept.detail: host_silence_step pauses the device and sets g_silence.waiting/taken (736-741). on_disconnected calls host_silence_off (420), but stop() (575-588, the player's own disconnect or an invite via autostart 657-660) does not. After set_phase(Off), frame() returns before host_silence_step (760-761), so the device pause 'coop_host_silent' and g_silence stay until some later session's first frame lifts them (713-720). That unpause then lands in a different context.
kept.fix: Call host_silence_off(SilenceEnd::StoppedWaiting) in stop() before set_phase(Off), or move it into set_phase(Off) so every end path takes it.

kept.title: log_allowed exists in 12 copies with 3 different budgets
kept.detail: `++n <= 20 || n % 100 == 0`: requests 99, events 143 and 140 (spawn_wait), entities 938 (by ref), death 184, money 144, sound 148. `count <= 10 || count % 100 == 0`: checkpoints 87, checkpoint_sources 116, debug 48, rest 58, script 213, sync_api 156. Plus requests note_bad (114, first 10) and worldstate refuse_log_allowed.
kept.fix: Add one `struct LogBudget { u32 n = 0; u32 first; bool allow() { return ++n <= first || n % 100 == 0; } };` in a Core header and use one instance per budget. Keep the two first-N values as named constants if they are intentional.

kept.title: put_vec/get_vec copied in three files
kept.detail: coop_events.cpp:200-211, coop_objects.cpp:240-253 and coop_requests.cpp:3747-3758 write and read an Fvector through float[3]. entities does the same inline (write_placement 146-149, client_on_snapshot 1817-1819), and events host_flush does too (1092-1093).
kept.fix: Add `inline void put(Writer&, const Fvector&)` and `inline Fvector get_fvector(Reader&)` once in an engine-side header next to coop_writer.h, and delete the copies.

kept.title: Avatar section in 3 places; is_remote_driven does a strcmp per creature, twice per frame
kept.detail: sync::is_remote_driven uses `xr_strcmp(obj->cNameSect(), "coop_player_avatar")` (390). coop_join.cpp:106 has its own kProxySection literal. world::avatar_section() (coop_world.cpp:25-29) with is_player_character(obj) (77) already does a shared_str pointer compare. is_remote_driven runs via remote::is_remote_creature, which is called twice per creature per frame (coop_remote.cpp:266 in update_cl, then 280 in apply).
kept.fix: Use world::is_player_character(obj) in is_remote_driven, use world::avatar_section() in join, and call is_remote_creature once in update_cl by passing the result to apply.
kept.correction: Confirmed: is_remote_driven does an xr_strcmp per call (coop_sync.cpp:390), join has its own kProxySection literal (coop_join.cpp:106, used at 495 and 551), and update_cl/apply call is_remote_creature twice (coop_remote.cpp:255, 280). However, world::avatar_section() is in an anonymous namespace in coop_world.cpp (24-29) and cannot be called from join. Either export it, or use world::is_player_character(e) at join:495 and export the name for the spawn at 551. Payoff is low.

kept.title: to_host_id/to_local_id are identity wrappers over join::to_host/to_local
kept.detail: `u16 to_host_id(u16 id) { return id == kNoId ? kNoId : join::to_host(id); }` (178-179). join::to_local (coop_join.h:214-220) already returns 0xffff for 0xffff: if my_proxy is 0xffff it returns host_id; otherwise 0xffff is neither 0 nor p. So the guard never changes the result, and there are dozens of call sites in requests.
kept.fix: Delete both wrappers and call join::to_host/to_local directly (or keep them in join with a comment that kNoId maps to itself).

kept.title: Dead entities API: host_on_event, host_send_subtree, host_begin_join/host_end_join
kept.detail: host_on_event(NET_Packet&) {} (2296) is declared in coop_entities.h:44 and has no caller anywhere in xrGame/xrCoop. host_send_subtree (2103-2106) is undeclared and uncalled, a pass-through to send_subtree with a 4-line work-package comment (2099-2102). host_begin_join/host_end_join (2166-2167) are empty and called only from sync (coop_sync.cpp:214, 219).
kept.fix: Delete all four along with their declaration and calls.

kept.title: Empty on_peer_joined chain: sync::on_peer_joined and join::on_peer_joined do nothing
kept.detail: coop_manager.cpp:349-351 calls `join::on_peer_joined(p)` (empty, coop_join.cpp:4034) under `active() && mode().decides_world()` and then `sync::on_peer_joined(p)` (empty, coop_sync.cpp:159).
kept.fix: Delete both functions and both calls. The callback keeps only its log line.

kept.title: Server-layer map-server stats declared in the Core manager header and registered by Core console
kept.detail: coop_manager.h:155-157 declares mapserver_stats_frame/mapserver_stats_register_console, which are implemented in srv/coop_mapserver_stats.cpp. The Core coop_console.cpp:252 calls mapserver_stats_register_console(), so the Core reaches into the Server layer (docs/MODES.md: the Core knows no mode).
kept.fix: Declare them in a srv header and register the console command from the server mode's boot or install (where coop_srv_mode.cpp:655 already calls the frame).
kept.correction: The layer leak is confirmed (coop_manager.h:155-157, coop_console.cpp:252). The fix location is wrong: the mode's install runs at session start, which is too late, because commands must exist before user.ltx is read (coop_console.cpp:257 comment, Layer::register_console contract at coop_mode.h:367-368). The existing route is ServerLayer::register_console, reached through register_layers_console (coop_mode.cpp:72-76, srv/coop_srv_console.cpp:9-10). The frame call can stay in srv/coop_srv_mode.cpp:655. dedicated::register_console (coop_console.cpp:253, with the Core including srv/coop_dedicated.h at line 18) is the same leak and should move with it.

kept.title: 'World replaced' is a hidden fan-out inside join::host_watch_world
kept.detail: On a new world generation, join resets other modules itself: objects::reset() (4331), levels::host_world_replaced() (4332), and its own gate, choosers and transition. Other modules discover the new world on their own (items via Device.dwPrecacheFrame at coop_items.cpp:2452, entities and events by dropping recorded events when !world_up). There is no single 'world replaced' event.
kept.fix: Add sync::on_world_replaced() as one list, next to reset() in the module table, called from host_watch_world. Move objects::reset and levels::host_world_replaced there.

kept.title: coop_entities.cpp (2654) mixes replication, roster repair and ~600 lines of pose diagnostics
kept.detail: Host events + snapshots (73-243, 816-876), pose diagnostics P101/P103 (285-472: watch_decider, motion_name, describe_slots), creature flags/hands/attachments apply (474-814), roster/reconcile (941-1220), client apply of spawn/switch/squads (1226-1960), entity requests (1949-2066), mirror pose driving and its lines (2430-2683, describe_copy 2704-2731).
kept.fix: Split into coop_entities.cpp (events, spawn/switch apply), coop_snapshots.cpp (host_send_snapshots, client_on_snapshot, interpolate, drive_mirror, flags/attachments), coop_roster.cpp (collect_rows .. client_reconcile), coop_pose_diag.cpp (watch_decider, describe_copy, motion_name, watch_pose lines).
kept.correction: The file has 2798 lines, not 2654. The pose diagnostics come to about 285 lines, not about 600: 285-472 (parts_of, motion_name, describe_slots, watch_creature, watch_entity, watch_decider), watch_pose 2546-2611 and describe_copy 2704-2731. motion_valid, placeholder_of, part_bare, play_own_idle and drive_parts (2430-2545) are behaviour, not diagnostics: they play the puppet's own idle when no snapshot drives a partition. They must stay with drive_mirror in the snapshots file, not move to coop_pose_diag.cpp.

kept.title: About 714 comment lines in this lane narrate history (dates, reviews, R/F/W/TZ ids, builds)
kept.detail: Regex count of comment lines with 'Live 20xx-', 'review', R/F/W/TZ/P ids, 'build NN', 'Ruling', 'protocol N', 'round N': join 219, requests 167, entities 83, session 59, sync 48, items 45, events 34, manager 34, objects 24. Examples: coop_manager.cpp:32-40 ('Was 120 s', 'live 2026-11-01'), 851-855 ('TZ R38 (RL-N8HP-7FDG)...'), coop_objects.cpp:2440-2441 ('build 58, LNK2001'), coop_join.cpp:2925 ('2026-10-24: the group goes...'), coop_sync.cpp:238-245.
kept.fix: Rewrite each comment into the current rule and why ('a crashed client must look silent within 10 s'). Move dates, ids and incident numbers to git messages and vault notes. Do it file by file together with the splits above.

kept.title: Host copies and sorts every player's inventory id list every frame
kept.detail: items::frame calls host_track_proxies(now) every frame without a timer (2507). For each player slot it does `xr_vector<u16> cur = pe->children; std::sort(...)` (2165-2166), building a new vector per player per frame (GAMMA inventories have 100-300 items). It also builds an `xr_set<u16> seen` (2147), and MSVC's std::set allocates its head node in the constructor. The comparison at `it->second == cur` is almost always equal.
kept.fix: Keep the previous unsorted children copy per proxy and compare it to pe->children first (same size and memcmp). Only on difference copy+sort into a persistent scratch vector. Replace `seen` with a fixed bitset over kMaxPeerSlots proxies, or skip it when nothing changed. Results and timing stay the same.

kept.title: Release build walks every object and the level ALife registry every 10 s for pose diagnostics
kept.detail: watch_decider (437-472) runs on every decider. Every mirror_pose::kRoundMs it iterates Level().Objects, and per stalker it runs capture_anims, parts_of and `ka->ID_Cycle_Safe("death_init")` (394), a motion lookup by name that builds a shared_str each call. Then it walks ai().alife().graph().level().objects() including squad members (459-470). This is a periodic main-thread spike whose only output is log lines.
kept.fix: Cache the placeholder MotionID per visual (a map keyed by IKinematicsAnimated* or the visual name). Spread the walk over frames (a slice per frame), or gate it behind a coop_diag console flag that is off by default.
kept.correction: watch_decider (coop_entities.cpp:437-472) runs only where leads_level() is true, i.e. on the co-op host and on map servers, not on every decider (the dedicated world server has leads_level=false). It runs once every kRoundMs = 10 s (coop_mirror_pose_rules.h:34), not every frame, and ID_Cycle_Safe('death_init') runs only for live stalkers. Its cost is unmeasured and probably below 1 ms per 10 s. Keep it as a measure-first, low-payoff item. Turning it off by default changes only log output.

kept.title: Broadcast builds a separate ENet packet (malloc + memcpy) for every peer
kept.detail: Session::broadcast loops m_joined and m_trunks and calls send_packet per peer (2471-2477). Each call makes net::Transport::make_packet -> enet_packet_create(nullptr, 2+n) + memcpy (coop_transport.cpp:322-347). net::to_peer from Mode::deliver does the same per peer through Session::send. ENet reference-counts packets, so one packet can be enet_peer_send'ed to many peers.
kept.fix: When NetSim is off and the lane is not Bulk (no per-connection ByteCounter), create the packet once and enet_peer_send it to every target under one g_io lock. Keep the per-peer may_send filter and count_sent. Add a Session::send_many(ids, lane, type, payload) so deliver/to_players use it too.

kept.title: Each received packet is copied into a new vector, then wrapped in make_shared, and its Handler copied
kept.detail: take_event copies packet bytes into Event::bytes and destroys the ENet packet (273-274). game_message wraps the moved vector in std::make_shared (coop_session.cpp:897, one more allocation), and run_handler copies the std::function from m_handlers after a second map lookup (451-466, the first lookup is at 890). There are at least two heap allocations per incoming game message.
kept.fix: Keep the ENetPacket alive in a refcounted holder (the Packet RAII type exists) and pass a span. Alternatively allocate the shared buffer once in take_event (allocate_shared with the bytes) so game_message only moves the pointer. Look up the handler once and store the iterator, or a pointer, if handlers are not re-registered meanwhile.
kept.correction: Confirmed: there are two allocations per incoming message, the copy into Event::bytes (coop_transport.cpp:273-274) and make_shared (coop_session.cpp:897), plus the emit closure. The second map lookup is also real (890 and 461). Drop the part of the fix that stops copying the handler: the copy is deliberate, and coop_session.cpp:451 says 'copy: the handler may re-register itself', so keeping an iterator or pointer would break that. Copying a small lambda std::function usually stays in the small buffer anyway. Payoff is low.

kept.title: Host events flush constructs and frees 2 maps + 1 set and takes a lock every frame, even when idle
kept.detail: host_flush (1054-1068) declares local xr_map<u16,ParentChange>, xr_map<u16,Fvector>, xr_vector, xr_vector and xr_set every frame and swaps them under g_lock. MSVC's std::map/set allocate their sentinel node in the default constructor, so that is 3 allocations and frees per frame on the host with nothing to send.
kept.fix: Under the lock, return early when all five containers are empty. Alternatively keep static scratch containers, swap, process, clear and swap back so capacity is reused.

kept.title: Roster step computes the 'mapless' rows and hash even when the mode has no link to send them to
kept.detail: host_reconcile runs every kStepMs (312 ms) and always calls collect_rows(bucket, rows, &mapless) (1115). For every inventory item mapless_row runs held_by_the_living and items::state_digest a second time (1051-1058). It then hashes and calls mode().deliver_links (1125-1127), which in co-op sends to nobody (comment 1124: the host player's link does not take it).
kept.fix: Add Mode::has_links(Msg) (or reuse bridge_takes) and compute mapless only when it is true. The co-op host then does half the row work.

kept.title: FNV-1a hash implemented three times
kept.detail: objects::hash_str (coop_objects.cpp:212-218, 32-bit), reconcile::kind_of (xrCoop/coop_reconcile.h:91-98, 32-bit then folded) and Manager's fnv1a (coop_manager.cpp:131-140, 64-bit).
kept.fix: Add one `constexpr uint32_t fnv1a32(const char*)` and `uint64_t fnv1a64(const void*, size_t, seed)` in an xrCoop header. kind_of keeps its fold on top.
kept.correction: FNV-1a is written out at least 8 times, not 3: coop_objects.cpp:212-218, xrCoop/coop_reconcile.h:91-98, coop_manager.cpp:131-140 (64-bit), xrCoop/coop_gear.h:65-69, xrCoop/coop_item_tags.h:185-186, xrCoop/coop_zone_path_rules.h:199-201, xrCoop/coop_protocol.cpp:425 (64-bit) and xrCoop/coop_session.cpp:2824. Several feed wire or compared values (reconcile kinds, zone paths, the manifest), so the shared helper must produce byte-identical results and keep each site's fold or seed.

kept.title: ApplyGuard duplicates the public ClientApply RAII
kept.detail: `struct ApplyGuard { ApplyGuard() { ++g_applying; } ~ApplyGuard() { --g_applying; } }` (1220-1224) and `ClientApply::ClientApply() { ++g_applying; }` / `~ClientApply() { --g_applying; }` (2403-2404) are the same guard. Both are used in the same file (1877 and 1458 vs 674 and 780).
kept.fix: Delete ApplyGuard and use ClientApply everywhere.

kept.title: Two find_entity functions with the same name and different meaning
kept.detail: items::find_entity (coop_items.cpp:313-318) looks only in the ALife registry. events::find_entity (coop_events.cpp:1127-1137) looks in ALife and falls back to Level().Server->ID_to_entity. requests calls events::find_entity (783, 898). The same name returning different objects for non-ALife entities is a trap for the next edit.
kept.fix: Rename to alife_entity(id) and server_entity(id) (or have one function with an explicit fallback flag) and put them in one header.

kept.title: swap_values re-implements std::swap
kept.detail: `template <typename T> void swap_values(T& a, T& b) { T t = a; a = b; b = t; }` (1820-1826) is used only by the role swap (4690-4719) on plain fields (Fvector, float, u32, struct).
kept.fix: Use std::swap and delete the template.

kept.title: entities::is_creature is a pass-through to remote::is_puppet_type
kept.detail: `bool is_creature(CGameObject* obj) { return remote::is_puppet_type(obj); }` (280-283), used once in host_send_snapshots (842). events and presence call remote::is_puppet_type directly (coop_events.cpp:855, 1028).
kept.fix: Call remote::is_puppet_type at 842 and delete is_creature.

kept.title: objects::now_ms() is an identity wrapper of mgr().now_ms()
kept.detail: `u64 now_ms() { return mgr().now_ms(); }` (220). It is the C++ twin of the Lua now() -> time_global() wrappers already reported. Neighbouring modules call mgr().now_ms() directly.
kept.fix: Replace it with mgr().now_ms() at the call sites, or read `const u64 now` once per frame function.

kept.title: sync facade functions forward to one call without a stated reason
kept.detail: `bool alife_frozen() { return net::client(); }` (401) and `bool intercept_local_spawn(CSE_Abstract* e) { return entities::intercept_local_spawn(e); }` (403). There may be a reason (stock hook files include only coop_sync.h), but nothing says so.
kept.fix: Either write one line saying 'stock hooks see only coop_sync.h' above them, or include coop_net.h/coop_entities.h at the hook sites and delete the facades.
kept.correction: alife_frozen has exactly one caller, the stock hook at alife_update_manager.cpp:112, which includes coop/coop_sync.h. That facade is justified and needs a one-line comment. intercept_local_spawn is not a facade: it has no caller anywhere in xrGame, xrCoop or xrEngine. The whole chain is dead: sync::intercept_local_spawn (coop_sync.cpp:403, coop_sync.h:45-47), entities::intercept_local_spawn (coop_entities.cpp:2406-2428, coop_entities.h:85-86), and its counters g_forwarded_spawns and g_blocked_spawns, which print_status (2771) always shows as 0. requests::client_forward_spawn keeps its other callers (coop_events.cpp:236, coop_requests.cpp:1738). Kind: dead.

kept.title: Entities' coop_reconcile cvar is registered in requests through an int& getter
kept.detail: requests::register_console registers `CMD4(CCC_Integer, "coop_reconcile", &entities::reconcile_switch(), 0, 1)` (4303). reconcile_switch() exists only to expose g_coop_reconcile (coop_entities.cpp:2342).
kept.fix: Register it in an entities::register_console() (or coop_console.cpp next to the other cvars) and drop the reference getter.

kept.title: 'Run under an optional EchoOf' written twice with duplicated calls
kept.detail: host_process_events calls host_send_spawn(e) in both branches, differing only by a scoped `levels::EchoOf` (220-226). events::relay does the same with net::host_broadcast (coop_events.cpp:1043-1052).
kept.fix: Add one helper in coop_levels.h, `template<class F> void with_echo(u16 echo, F&& f)` (std::optional<EchoOf>), and use it in both places.

kept.title: One process-wide recursive mutex for all ENet hosts
kept.detail: `std::recursive_mutex g_io` (31-34) guards every Transport. A map server has two (m_world and m_session), so the owner and the two keep-alive threads (1 ms tick, try_lock at 571) contend across unrelated hosts. Recursion is needed only because all_acked calls outgoing_idle under the lock (482-488). The static accessors (user/set_user/rtt_ms/...) lock the global because they have no instance.
kept.fix: Use a plain std::mutex per Transport, make the accessors members (Session always has m_tp), and add an unlocked outgoing_idle_locked() for all_acked. Keep enet_initialize refcounting under g_enet_mutex.

kept.title: Two command-line parsers; cmd_param checks only the first occurrence
kept.detail: cmd_param (91-107) does a single strstr. If an earlier, longer key with the same prefix is found it returns false without looking further, so `-coop_hostX ... -coop_host` would miss -coop_host. skip_keypress_on_load (876-881) uses raw strstr, which matches prefixes, and srv uses its own strstr (srv/coop_mapserver.cpp:570). No such key pair exists today, so this is latent.
kept.fix: Add one tokenizer `bool cmd_key(LPCSTR key, xr_string* value)` that loops over all occurrences with the word-boundary test, and use it in manager and srv.
kept.correction: The latent prefix bug in cmd_param (coop_manager.cpp:91-107) and the raw strstr in skip_keypress_on_load (876-881) are confirmed. No prefix pair reaches cmd_param today; -coop_load and -coop_load_hex exist, but they go through the srv parser. There are more than two parsers, and a correct one already exists: detail::find_key in xrCoop/srv/coop_dedicated_rules.h:63-70 loops over every occurrence with a word-boundary test, and xrCoop/srv/coop_mapserver_rules.h:148-160 has a third loop of its own. The fix should move find_key into a Core header and use it in the Manager, the dedicated rules and the map-server rules, rather than write a new tokenizer.

kept.title: coop_manager.cpp is the only non-UTF-8 file in the lane
kept.detail: An iconv check shows that coop_manager.cpp is not valid UTF-8. The byte at line 528 ('plan 2026-11-12 §2.2') is in a legacy codepage. The other ten files in scope are UTF-8.
kept.fix: Convert it to UTF-8, and have the build/check script reject non-UTF-8 sources.

kept.title: xrCoop/coop_mode.h included twice
kept.detail: It is included at line 5 and again at line 24 with a history comment ('F4 G11-2: only the process that leads its map...').
kept.fix: Delete line 24.

kept.title: Magic flag 0x80 in Action.flags
kept.detail: send_action tests `a.flags & 0x80 // local rider activation failed after the speculative spawn` (743). The other flags of the same field are named constants (kMoveLocal/kMoveTrade/kMovePos, 83-85).
kept.fix: Add `constexpr u8 kSpawnRiderFailed = 0x80;` next to the others and use it where the flag is set and tested.

kept.title: Redundant mode check after an early return
kept.detail: actor_hit_blocked returns at 1298-1299 when decides_world() || leads_level(), and then tests `mode().decides_world()` again inside the condition at 1300.
kept.fix: Remove `mode().decides_world() ||` from line 1300.

kept.title: Frame functions repeat the same call and gate on every line
kept.detail: join::frame calls mgr().now_ms() eight times (4438-4467). sync::frame has 14 separate `if (up)` / `if (!gap)` single-line gates (coop_sync.cpp:250-296).
kept.fix: Use `const u64 now = mgr().now_ms();` once in join::frame. In sync::frame, group the up-only and !gap passes into blocks, or let the module table (see the sync finding) carry the gate.
kept.correction: Calling now_ms() once in join::frame is not behaviour-neutral. host_board_step can reach host_release (coop_join.cpp:2933), whose Level().Send(M_CHANGE_LEVEL) at 2804 writes the save synchronously; the code itself re-reads now_ms() around it (2802-2812). With one cached `now`, the later host_load_step, host_held_step and arrival_step would get a time from before the save, possibly seconds old. Read the time again after host_board_step (and after any step that can block), or set behaviour_change=true. In sync::frame (coop_sync.cpp:250-296), only adjacent calls with the same gate may be merged, because the stated order matters (events after entities, reconcile after events, vehicles after objects::frame).

refuted.why: The race cannot happen in practice. Every caller of on_blocking_work runs on the main thread: CGamePersistent::Start (GamePersistent.cpp:190), OnDeviceResetBegin (325), LoadTitle (1008), CLevel::net_Stop (Level_network.cpp:128) and CALifeStorageManager::save (alife_storage_manager.cpp:59, which right after calls objects::host_flush_consumes, main-thread code). set_phase also runs on the main thread, so m_phase is never written and read at the same time. on_crash (any thread) reads only world_session(), which uses m_map_server, set once at a session's start. The only defect is the header comment 'Any thread' (coop_manager.h:158-163). Fix that comment, not the field types.

lua-world.summary: Слой мира (задания, NPC, спутники, арена, фракции) работает, но с точки зрения скорости и порядка он самый тяжёлый в Lua. Главная проблема по FPS: самые частые вызовы стока, которые идут на каждого NPC и каждую логику в каждом кадре (pick_section_from_condlist, try_switch, get_visible_value, npc_on_update маскировки, save_var), каждый раз заново спрашивают роль процесса через pcall и строят список игроков из движка. Ответ при этом меняется раз в секунды, а у модулей он уже лежит в host_on. Это чинится точечно, кэшем на кадр, и игрок ничего не заметит. Нашла два настоящих бага в минах. Заряды, которые поставил клиент, замирают, когда на сервере не осталось клиентов. А ветка совместимости со сборкой 56 при режиме доверия «log» даёт поставить мину без предмета. Сборку 56 движок к этой сессии всё равно не пустит: build_id должен совпадать. coop_tasks дорос до 4841 строки и упёрся в лимит Lua на 200 локальных переменных. Из-за этого функции разложены по таблицам host/ops и глобалам. В этом же файле лежит свой формат пакетов, хотя таких форматов в проекте уже три. Здесь же своя репликация состояния заданий раз в 0,5 с, которой место в движке или в coop.sync. Одни и те же помощники скопированы десятки раз: роли, список игроков (35 копий pcall(api.players)), ник (20), фракция без actor_ (14), загрузка модуля (9). Адаптеры модов разбросаны по coop_npc_*/coop_world_*/coop_quests_*, а не лежат в своих coop_mods_*. В комментариях около 309 строк истории (даты, раунды, ревью, сборки). Порядок такой: сначала кэш ролей и предикатов в горячих местах (пункты 1-6), потом баги мин, потом разрезать coop_tasks и свести форматы пакетов, помощников и адаптеры к одному.

kept.title: Adapter predicate calls host_with_clients() on every hooked NPC call
kept.detail: coop_npc_compat:1290 and 1292 pass `function() return host_on and P.host_with_clients() end` as `active` to coop_npc_adapters.install and coop_npc_phantoms.install. It is called inside hooks that run per NPC per update. visual_memory_manager.get_visible_value (coop_npc_adapters:136-139) runs per NPC per seen object. trade_manager.update (155-156) runs per trader update. The xr_danger corpse action (55-56) and the phantom wrappers (coop_npc_phantoms:37, 112, 135) are the same. host_with_clients (coop_npc_players:114-120) costs active() (a pcall), two coop_mode queries (each a pcall into the layer, coop_mode:195-202) and api.players(), which builds a fresh Lua table of player tables from C++ (107-111). Estimate: with Stealth Overhaul and 40 NPCs that see 5 objects each at 60 fps, about 12k calls/s, so roughly 50k pcalls and 12k table builds per second on the host. host_on already holds `installed and host_with_clients()`, refreshed every 250 ms (coop_npc_compat:1250).
kept.fix: Pass `function() return host_on end` to both installs, or expose `P.host_on()` from a per-frame cache in coop_npc_players.refresh(). Keep the 250 ms refresh where it is.

kept.title: try_switch resolves 'is this actor a remote player' with ~7 pcalls on every logic update
kept.detail: try_switch wraps xr_logic.try_switch_to_another_section (installed at 1701), which every scheme update of every NPC and restrictor calls. On the map authority, lines 751-756 call player_by_id(actor:id()) and own_actor() on every call, whether or not clients are connected, because host_on is not checked. That path runs P.peer_of (self_peer pcall, refresh), player_here (coop_mode.where pcall, P.self_peer pcall, coop_mode.actor_is_player pcall, own_actor with coop_mods_core.identity_obj, actor:alive, P.standing with pcall(api.life_of)) (614-628). P.active() at 739 and P.is_client() at 747 add more. In almost every call `actor` is this process's own actor and the answer is 'stock'.
kept.fix: Before the player lookup, take the stock path when the actor is the own actor: `local own = own_actor(); if own and actor:id() == own:id() then return orig.try_switch(npc, st, actor) end`. Keep the role answers in a per-frame snapshot (coop_npc_players.refresh) instead of asking coop_mode on each call.

kept.title: pick_section scans every condlist for 'offences' with fresh tables and 3 pcalls per evaluation
kept.detail: pick_section wraps xr_logic.pick_section_from_condlist (installed at 1705). With clients connected it calls coop_reputation.pick_offence for every evaluation (1269-1273). pick_offence (coop_reputation:65-77) first calls owns_reputation(), which is 3 pcalls (coop_reputation:7-9). It then allocates `offences = {}` and walks every line's checks and effects comparing names, then pcall(id_of, npc) and db.storage (1276-1277). on_info lines always fire (SWITCH_TESTS.on_info returns true, coop_npc_logic:589), so this runs for every logic object with an on_info line on every update. Condlists are parsed once and never change, so the verdict is constant per condlist table.
kept.fix: Cache the offence verdict per condlist table in a weak-keyed table (`offence_of[condlist] = offences or false`), as has_actor_conds already does for st.logic (560-572). Do not call owns_reputation per call: host_on already implies this process decides the map. Call id_of without pcall for game objects.

kept.title: team_try_switch allocates a table and two closures per logic object per update
kept.detail: For every object whose logic has actor conditions, each update builds `here = {npc, st, ost}` plus `function here.pos()` and `function here.near()` (678-687). On the host that is three allocations per call for many restrictors and NPCs, every frame.
kept.fix: Reuse one module-level scratch record: set npc/st/ost and clear pos/nearest at the start of each call. Make pos and near local functions that take the record (or compute pos up front, since it is cheap, and near lazily) so they are not closures.
kept.correction: The allocations are real (coop_npc_logic:678-687, host with clients only). The proposed module-level scratch record is not re-entrancy safe. The loop keeps using `here` after pick_and_switch, which runs condlist effects and switch_to_section. The same file already saves and restores transition_user around nested calls (transition_for), so nesting is expected. A nested team_try_switch would overwrite the shared record and the remaining tests would read another NPC, which changes behaviour. Use a depth-indexed pool, or pass npc/st/ost plus a per-depth cache. Payoff is low to medium.

kept.title: save_var wrapper does 2-3 pcalls and a closure on every save_var, single player included
kept.detail: _G.save_var is replaced on every machine with the coop exe, single player included: on_game_start only checks `api`. Each call evaluates client_live() first (active() pcall, coop_mode.decides_world pcall, api.is_live). It then calls is_my_actor(obj), which runs pcall(function ...) with a fresh closure (2413-2421). For actor keys it then calls host.var_own, which does a rawget and pcall(coop_quests_trust.note_own, ...) (1928-1936). Stock xr_logic, task scripts and GAMMA mods call save_var very often.
kept.fix: Put the cheap checks first: `if not active() then return orig(...) end`, then is_shared_key(k), then the actor check. Make is_my_actor pcall-free: `type(obj) == 'userdata' and obj:id() == AC_ID`, since game objects always have id(). Call note_own only for fact keys (coop_quests_trust.is_fact) and only on the deciding process.
kept.correction: The hot path is real, single player included: every actor save_var runs is_my_actor (a pcall plus a closure), then var_own (actor_pstor plus pcall(note_own)). The proposed fix changes behaviour in two places. (a) is_my_actor compares with db.actor:id(), which inside P.with_identity is the client's proxy. Using AC_ID would stop routing and recording those writes, so keep db.actor:id() and only drop the closure: `type(obj)=='userdata' and obj:id()==db.actor:id()` (stock save_var already calls obj:id()). (b) Calling note_own only when is_fact(k, v) misses deletions of table facts. note_own tests fact_key(k,v) or fact_key(k,old) (coop_quests_trust:200-202), so writing nil over an item_1_sec/target_id table would no longer clear own[k] or set no_fact. The gate must be is_fact(k,v) or is_fact(k, ps[k]). Gating var_own on active() is neutral in practice: save_state writes coop_task_facts only on the world authority, own_init adopts the pstor when no list exists, and every load is a new Lua state.

kept.title: Disguise npc_on_update: per NPC, per peer, per frame pcalls, option lookups and CTime allocations
kept.detail: guarded_npc_update pcalls npc_on_update for every NPC update. It is registered unconditionally (499), so single player with the coop exe pays it too (463-466). For every client in players_state the per-NPC body runs P.object_of_peer (2 pcalls plus object_by_id, coop_npc_players:213-220), tosox_enabled() (a mod lookup per NPC, 366), npc:see, in_disguise_zone (2 zone lookups) and game.get_game_time() CTime allocations (383, 406). A client stays in players_state while not disguised, because he reports every 30 s (82, 415). When he is disguised and seen, stay_factor and dist_factor each call opt() twice: pcall(ui_options.get) plus a string concat (296-308).
kept.fix: In host_tick (every 250 ms), resolve s.proxy once and read the options into s.opts; read tosox once at install. In guarded_npc_update, check `host_on and next(players_state)` before the pcall. Register npc_on_update only while players_state is not empty, as coop_npc_player_checks does for bribes (366-380).
kept.correction: The per-NPC, per-peer cost is confirmed while host_on is set and players_state is not empty. In single player it is only one pcall plus a return per NPC update. Do not keep the proxy game_object in s.proxy across 250 ms ticks: an avatar released or respawned in between leaves a stale userdata, which is a crash risk in X-Ray. Cache the avatar id per frame and resolve it with level.object_by_id. Reading the options in host_tick delays an options change by up to 250 ms, which nobody can see. Reading tosox once and gating on next(players_state) before the pcall are fine.

kept.title: Client-planted mines freeze when no client is connected
kept.detail: host_on = installed and P.host_with_clients() (834) gates host_mines_tick (835-837) and the npc_on_update/monster_on_update proximity checks (guard, 816-822, 899-900). `mines` holds only charges planted by clients (host_on_mine, 307), and they are saved and loaded (846-868). Once the last client leaves, or after a load with the host alone, timer charges never go off. Proximity charges also ignore NPCs, monsters and the host until a client joins again, and then they all go off at once.
kept.fix: Gate mine ticking on authority plus `next(mines) ~= nil`: `(coop_mode.decides_world() or coop_mode.leads_here()) and next(mines)`, not on 'has clients'. Keep host_on for the parts that really need clients.
kept.correction: The bug is confirmed: host_on gates both host_mines_tick and the near_mine guard (coop_npc_world:816-822, 834-837), and mines are saved and loaded (846-868), so client charges stay inert while the host is alone. One detail is wrong. When a client returns, only TIMER charges that are past their time go off together. Proximity charges still need a creature within TRIGGER_RADIUS, though an NPC already standing on one sets it off at its next update. The fix must not change the shared guard() that on_container_opened also uses (see finding 9). behaviour_change stays true.

kept.title: Mine request without item id plants a free charge in trust mode 'log' (dead build-56 branch)
kept.detail: host_on_mine treats `t.i == nil` as 'a client of build 56' (282-285): trust_pass('mine_item_id', false, ...) returns true in mode log, and the charge is created without checking or removing any item. coop_trust.pass returns `not refuse` (coop_trust:58-74), and configs/mod_system_coop_trust.ltx sets `default = log`. A build-56 client cannot join: the engine rejects a different build_id and content fingerprint (engine/src/xrCoop/coop_session.cpp:1232-1240). So the branch only serves a modified client, which can plant unlimited mines. The matching client-side compat (113-118, 139-149, 'a host of build 56') is dead too.
kept.fix: Refuse a request without `i` (no plant, answer 'no'). Delete the build-56 comments and branches. Keep the 15 s client timeout only if a lost answer is still a real case, and describe it that way.
kept.correction: This is not a separate exploit. In trust mode 'log' a modified client can just as well send a bogus `i`: mine_item_check fails, trust_pass('mine_item') returns true (coop_trust:58-74), and the charge is planted without consuming an item. That is the same outcome as the t.i==nil branch and is the deliberate 'log' policy. What is real: the build-56 branches and comments (coop_npc_world:282-285, 113-118, 139-149) are dead, because the Hello build_id and content_fp checks reject such clients (coop_session.cpp:1232-1246). Deleting the branch alone changes nothing (a nil i fails mine_item_check and gets the same log-mode outcome). Refusing the request changes behaviour only for modified clients. Keep the 15 s client timeout for lost answers (coop_events_lost exists) and describe it that way. Recategorise as kind dead, behaviour_change false if only deleted.

kept.title: host_mines_tick is O(mines^2 x players) every 250 ms
kept.detail: For each active proximity mine the loop calls near_mine(p) for every player (350-351), and near_mine itself walks all mines again (328-333) using distance_to, a sqrt (331). The result is the same as one pass per player.
kept.fix: Loop over P.everyone() once, outside the mine loop (each player checks all mines), and compare distance_to_sqr with TRIGGER_RADIUS^2. blast() already sets active=false, so the triggers stay identical.

kept.title: pcall per NPC and monster update even when there are no client mines
kept.detail: npc_on_update and monster_on_update are registered through guard() (816-822, 899-900). With clients connected, every creature update does pcall(near_mine), which returns at `next(mines) == nil` (325).
kept.fix: Check `next(mines)` in the guard before the pcall, or register both callbacks only while proximity charges exist. coop_npc_player_checks:366-380 uses that self-registering pattern.
kept.correction: guard() is shared with mine_blame and on_container_opened (coop_npc_world:898, 905). Putting a next(mines) check inside guard() would stop on_container_opened from recording mine_item.opened, which mine_item_check uses, and that changes behaviour. Add the check only in a separate guard for the npc_on_update and monster_on_update near_mine registrations.

kept.title: Rank place recomputed with full ALife walks every 2 s near the Snitch and on every PDA open
kept.detail: On a client within 25 m of bar_informator_mlr before top_10_task_started, prefetch_rank probes every 500 ms and sends RANK_REQ every 2 s (121-131, 142-153). On the world authority each request runs stock pda.calculate_rankings (rank_place/read_rankings 36-50), which likely walks all ALife objects. coop_quests_pda host_on_rank_req (54-98), triggered by every PDA open on a client (coop_world_compat:67-75), runs calculate_rankings and then a second walk over ids 1..65534 (91-98). The two files compute the place differently. quests.rank_req has no host-side rate limit (only the client throttles it); pda_req has set_limit at coop_quests_pda:451.
kept.fix: Keep one rank helper (coop_quests_stock.rank_place) whose calculate_rankings result is cached for a few seconds on the authority, and drop the 65534 walk (place = index in the sorted list). Add a host-side set_limit for quests.rank_req. Read the requester's rank from his own character on the host, not from the rank he sends (t.r, coop_quests_pda:88).
kept.correction: Several details are wrong. coop_quests_stock RANK_REQ already has a host-side limit: C().set_limit(RANK_REQ, 2, 0.5) at coop_quests_stock:244. coop_world_compat:67-75 calls calculate_rankings locally, and the coop_quests_pda wrapper (178-190) turns that into a rank_req at most every 5 s (RANK_COOLDOWN). What is right: quests.rank_req (coop_quests_pda:1055, through qc.on and coop_main.add_event_handler) has no host-side limit, and each request runs calculate_rankings plus a 1..65534 sim:object walk (91-98). The fix 'drop the walk, place = index in the sorted list' changes behaviour: get_coc_ranking_list is cut to the array size (coop_quests_stock:36-38 and its overwritten-slot logic at 54-69), so a player outside the list would get no place. Keep the walk, or compute it once per cached ranking. Caching calculate_rankings for a few seconds and adding set_limit('rank_req') are fine. Reading the requester's rank on the host instead of t.r is a trust fix that changes behaviour and should be marked so. The ALife walk inside stock calculate_rankings is not verifiable here (pda.script is not in the repo).

kept.title: Task mirror rescans the whole pstor and re-encodes every task every 0.5 s
kept.detail: With clients, host_scan runs every SCAN_MS = 500 (4634-4639). scan_vars walks every key of the actor pstor and does k:find/k:sub at every '_' (695-720). task_record then runs pcall with a fresh closure per task (724-728) and pack() with a sort twice (732-737), and compares the result string to host.sent. That is a lot of string and table garbage every half second, whether anything changed or not.
kept.fix: Track dirty keys: the save_var wrapper (4603) already sees every actor pstor write and can mark task ids and shared keys dirty. Stage and status changes pass through the patched task_manager methods (4400-4536). Scan only dirty tasks and keep a slow full pass together with the 10 s digest list as a safety net. Read stage/status/giver without the closure pcall.
kept.correction: The claim that the save_var wrapper sees every actor pstor write is wrong. host_on_var writes ps[k] directly (coop_tasks:903-933, comment at 1927), and a load fills the pstor without save_var. Dirty tracking must also hook host_on_var and the load. Otherwise such changes reach clients only with the slow full pass, a visible delay that changes behaviour. The rest is confirmed: scan_vars (695-720), the closure pcall (724-728), pack sorting twice (732-737), SCAN_MS=500 (103).

kept.title: coop_tasks (4841 lines) is at Lua's 200-locals limit and mixes ten jobs
kept.detail: Comments say helpers were moved into `host`/`ops` tables and module globals only because 'the chunk is at Lua's limit of 200 locals' (378, 524, 579, 601-602, 4543). That leaks functions such as far_of, rep_share_rule and peer_in_session into the public module API. The file holds a payload codec (192-300), group inventories (376-460), task audience (598-690), the Lua state mirror (692-900, 3595-3990), request handling and verdicts (900-2400), rewards and money (2400-3230), party items (3230-3595), news (4141-4325), the task_manager patch (4369-4537), guides (4539-4596) and start/update.
kept.fix: Split it by job. coop_tasks keeps the ownership and recipient API (taker, recipient, with_task_owner). Separate files: coop_tasks_mirror (state to clients), coop_tasks_requests (client ops and verdicts), coop_tasks_rewards (money, items, effects), coop_tasks_items (party inventory), coop_tasks_news. The codec goes to the shared one (next finding).

kept.title: Three payload codecs for one event channel
kept.detail: coop_main.encode/decode (coop_main:89-138): flat, numbers via tostring. coop_tasks esc/enc_scalar/enc_flat/pack/unpack_payload/digest (196-299): one nesting level, %.17g, its own escape set. coop_quests_core ser/des (157-235): nested. All three wrap the same api.send_event string payload. coop_core_world uses yet another accessor, codec() (1068, 1135).
kept.fix: Keep one codec (nested, %.17g) in coop_main, or better a C++ one in the engine. coop_tasks and coop_quests_core call it. Clients and host always run the same build (build_id check), so the format can change in one step.
kept.correction: 'Change the format in one step' misses saved data. host.fx_wait holds pack() strings (coop_tasks:2451-2457), save_effects writes them to m_data.coop_task_fx.wait (4727-4738), and host_resend_effects sends them again after a load (2476-2480). A new codec must decode or migrate those saved strings, or pending task rewards from older saves are lost on the clients. Also, coop_core_world codec() (84-86) only returns coop_main; it is an accessor, not a fourth codec.

kept.title: Continuous shared state replicated with self-made events instead of coop.sync
kept.detail: The lane replicates long-lived state by hand, while coop.sync is in use next door (coop_world_fx, coop_world_weather, coop_world_fight, coop_npc_effects, coop_trader_reputation). Cases: coop_tasks Lua task mirror (coop_tl / coop_tl_list / coop_tl_req / coop_tv, 85-93, with scan, digest, parts and resync 692-900, 3791-3940); coop_quests_party mirror_tick, a key/number map resent whole when the player count grows (349-362); coop_quests_missions guide state (822-837); coop_npc_companions_hire push_counts with its own `told` table per peer (192-209); coop_npc_disguise meter every 2 s (435). Owner rule: replication belongs to the engine and new shared state goes through coop.sync.
kept.fix: Use world-scope keys for the task mirror, party mirror and guide, and player-scope keys for hire counts and disguise meter. The engine already handles late join and resync, so delete the digest lists, resend-on-join and told bookkeeping.
kept.correction: These are instances of the already known deviation 'send_event in 21 scripts' (coop_tasks, coop_quests_core and coop_npc_players are among the files that call send_event), so refer to that item instead of reporting a new one. The fix is also wrong for the task mirror: host.send_task (coop_tasks:650-656) sends a task's state only to its audience (host.aud_sees). World-scope coop.sync keys would show every task to every client, a behaviour change; it needs audience-scoped or player-scope keys. The claim that the engine already handles late join and resync for such keys is not verified here.

kept.title: Role and player helpers re-implemented per file (35 copies of pcall(api.players))
kept.detail: Same helpers in several files: coop_tasks active/self_peer/players/to_host_id/to_local_id/has_clients/send (148-181, 586-596); coop_quests_core active/is_client/client_live/self_peer/players/host_party/to_host_id/to_local_id (35-85); coop_core_world in_session/leads_level/live_client/host_id/local_id (88-112); coop_npc_players (70-132); coop_mods_core (95-128). host_party (qc:70-76), host_with_clients (P:114-120) and coop_tasks world_active()+has_clients() are the same predicate. pcall(api.players) appears in 35 scripts, in the lane: coop_tasks:170, coop_quests_core:55, coop_core_world:201, coop_rest:259, coop_parity:341, coop_transition_route:165, coop_checkpoints:103. coop_trader_reputation:52 calls api.players() without pcall, and coop_tasks:176 and coop_core_world:107 call to_host_id without pcall where others use one, so errors behave differently.
kept.fix: Keep one roles/players module (coop_npc_players, or a small coop_roles) with a per-frame cached players list and role snapshot, and have every file call it.

kept.title: host_on polled 4 Hz in nine files, each building the players list; role queries are pcalls
kept.detail: `host_on = installed and P.host_with_clients()` with its own 250 ms timer appears in coop_npc_combat:406, coop_npc_companions:1585, coop_npc_compat:1250, coop_npc_disguise:451, coop_npc_effects:632, coop_npc_logic:1736, coop_npc_meet:752, coop_npc_world:834 and coop_world_fx:577. Each poll calls api.players(), which builds a table. Every coop_mode.* answer is current() plus a pcall into the layer (coop_mode:195-202), and hot code asks actor_is_player, leads_here and decides_world per call (for example nearest() at coop_npc_players:307).
kept.fix: Compute players(), host_with_clients, actor_is_player, leads_here and decides_world once per frame in coop_npc_players.refresh() (it already caches others/everyone per frame, 146-174). Expose P.host_on() and P.roles(), and delete the nine private timers.

kept.title: 75 actor_on_update callbacks, each with its own throttle; several run pcalls every frame
kept.detail: 73 non-adapter scripts register 75 actor_on_update callbacks, and each one repeats `if now < next_tick then return end; next_tick = now + X` plus pcall and report. Unthrottled per-frame work with pcalls: coop_quests_missions:931-940 (two pcalls), coop_quests_party:851-859, coop_quests_trust:830-833, coop_npc_presence:401 (update_safespawn with coop_mode pcalls, 344-386), coop_bounty:663-664 (update_target_link with role checks before the throttle), coop_quests_pda:918-922 (session_key() with a pcall closure and string concat every frame while a claim waits, 901-909), coop_npc_companions_ui:228-231, and coop_tasks dead_tick (4660-4674), which AddUniqueCall runs every frame forever with active() and alive pcalls.
kept.fix: Add one scheduler in coop_main, `coop_main.every(ms, tag, fn)`, that does one time check per entry and one shared pcall/report. Modules register intervals instead of raw actor_on_update. Only call dead_tick while the actor is dead: register it on death and return true when alive.

kept.title: Investigation probe ships in release and scans all online stalkers every second
kept.detail: The header describes a one-off investigation from a test on 2026-11-12 (4-8). On the authority with clients, every second scan() walks db.OnlineStalkers and, per stalker, calls P.is_proxy, pcall closures for alive/best_enemy and community() twice (69-86, 88-95) until 60 lines are written. It only writes log lines.
kept.fix: Put it behind the debug switch (coop_debug command or cvar), or delete it and keep explain() inside coop_debug_server.

kept.title: Reputation logging wrapper and per-second poll during fights
kept.detail: ensure_rep_line wraps game_statistics.increment_reputation (1611-1620), and route_rep_line (1585-1595) and rep_tick (1597-1609, called every second from actor_on_update at 2121) exist only to write diagnostic log lines about reputation during a fight.
kept.fix: Remove them, or move them to the debug tools.

kept.title: Mod adapters live in coop_npc_*/coop_world_*/coop_quests_* instead of one coop_mods_<mod> file each
kept.detail: coop_npc_compat: schemes_ai_gamma, night_mutants, visual_memory_manager, weapon_cover_tilt, gameplay_peace_zone, SKD, hxf, grok_*, smr_civil_war (REWRITES 62-100, installs 1293-1301). coop_npc_adapters: schemes_ai_gamma, stealth, trader_autoinject, mob_trade, grok_no_npc_friendly_fire. coop_npc_player_checks: xrs_facer, axr_stalker_panic, xr_bribe. coop_npc_relations: tasks_defense (setfenv 385-394), tasks_skyfall (249-269). coop_npc_presence: safespawn (388-412). coop_npc_companions: game_fast_travel (985-1013). coop_npc_companions_ui: grok_companions_no_ammo (193-205). coop_world_compat: TB safe zones, ui_hud_dotmarks (50-156). coop_world_fx_mods: nta_utils, Sabaoth, X8 door, skinning (276-291, 674-687). coop_quests_missions: tasks_guide (708). coop_quests_party: tasks_measure (819). coop_quests_story: drx_da_main (624). P12 asks for one adapter file per mod.
kept.fix: Move each mod's code into coop_mods_<mod>.script and leave coop_npc_*/coop_world_* with the stock-game logic only.

kept.title: Runtime source rewrites and setfenv on stock/mod functions
kept.detail: REWRITES (62-100) string-replace mod source (hxf_tough_important_npcs, grok_additional_storyline_npc_invincible, grok_killing_friends_reduces_goodwill, smr_civil_war) and recompile it at load. wrap_actor_friend_hit gives stock _g CActor__BeforeHitCallback a new environment with setfenv (1218-1233). coop_npc_relations does setfenv on tasks_defense.barrier_defense_available (385-394). This is the same class of hack as the known PBA rewrite, in another file. All of it serves one question: is the attacker a player? That belongs to the engine.
kept.fix: Have the engine answer 'is this draftsman a player character' in the hit and death callbacks the mods already receive (or one coop_npc_is_player_id hook), and delete the source rewrites and setfenv. Until then, move each one into its mod's coop_mods_ file.
kept.correction: The hack class is confirmed (coop_npc_compat REWRITES 62-100, setfenv 1218-1233, coop_npc_relations 385-394). The engine fix cannot remove the rewrites, though.
