kept.fix: Delete them, and the header line in coop_economy_group.

kept.title: Three copies of 'wrap a class method once, again if a mod replaced it'
kept.detail: take (398-420), take_guard (456-468) and watch_price (474-500) each repeat the same bookkeeping: current = cls[name], ours = wrapped[cls], return when ours[name] == current, build the wrapper, store it in ours and cls, stats.wraps++. Only the wrapper factory differs.
kept.fix: Write one local function wrap_once(cls, name, make) -> bool and have the three callers pass their factory.

kept.title: start_step copied in five economy files (and more outside)
kept.detail: Identical apart from the tag string: coop_economy_group 710, mdata 1851, money 620, travel 713, world 340. Outside this lane it is also in coop_core_chat 637, coop_core_player 392 and coop_faction 497. All of them guard on_game_start steps with pcall + printf.
kept.fix: Add coop_economy_core.start_step(tag, what, f) (or one helper in coop_main) and call it from all of them.
kept.correction: The scope is much wider than eight files. The same start_step body exists in about 30 more scripts (coop_mods_hf 1948, coop_mods_items 1459, mags 586, misc 1215, nta 973, pdata 449, perks 445, radio 912, quests_core 845, quests_fetch 689, rest 1141, saves 638, progress_check 739, settings_mods 15, and others), plus variants with a different tag or reporter (voice_fx 245, settings_cvars 156, npc_player_checks 383, world_views 395). The shared helper therefore belongs in coop_main (or another Core util), not in coop_economy_core, and each file's log tag must stay the same.

kept.title: axr_options accessor cfg() duplicated in menu and debug window
kept.detail: coop_debug_ui 207-214 and coop_menu 137-144 are byte-identical (rawget axr_main, load via _G, return .config). coop_menu_kit is already the shared helper module of both windows.
kept.fix: Move it to coop_menu_kit.cfg() and use it from both.

kept.title: Comments narrate history (dates, review numbers, TZ Rnn, 'was')
kept.detail: Lines with a date, an Rnn/TZ reference or a 'was'-style word, per file: economy_mdata 15/16/10, menu_char 12/0/7, core_hud 8/13/1, trade_window 8/10/13, hud_transition 7/4/3, menu 5/0/3. Examples: trade_window 3, 16, 29, 31, 231, 297, 422, 470, 548, 566 ('Review of 2026-11-25 (lua_flow#3)', 'TZ R92', 'W4 of the R92 review'); economy_core RULES 27-38 ('owner 2026-11-16', '(R-10.2)', 'The rule was travel_time and on by default'); hud_layout 20-23, 49 ('was ~0.6', 'TZ 6.13, R56 / R61', an E:\coop-hud-design path); core_hud 2, 11, 14, 68, 295, 1195 ('W4 core, reworked by W6', 'F3a task 6', 'Live 2026-10-24'); mdata 1256-1258 ('TZ v2 6.4 row 6, 2026-11-18', 'Round 2 (F4)'); item_journal 3; menu_char 23-35 ('Protocol 9 (owner, 2026-10-23...)').
kept.fix: Keep only the current rule and why in the comments. Move dates, review ids and the story to git and the vault notes, starting with trade_window, economy_core RULES, hud_layout DEFAULTS and core_hud.

kept.title: Mixed header styles: a Russian layer marker in English files, tags as descriptions
kept.detail: 62 coop_*.script start with '-- Ядро: без проверок режима (docs/MODES.md)'. In this lane: trade_window 1, credit 1, credit_events 1, credit_loot 1, credit_misc 1, pda_kills 1, hud3_fonts 1, hud_depth 1. Others use an English '-- Core: ...' (pda_marks_local 1) or a --[[ ]] block, and the rest of these files is English. tools/check_layers.py does not read this marker. Some files' only description is a work tag: credit_events 2 'Dev 57 G9-2.', credit_loot 2 'Dev 57 G9-3.', item_entity_state 1 'R32 W8:'.
kept.fix: Use one English header form for all coop_*.script: the --[[ ]] block with name, purpose, layer and API. Replace the work tags with what the file does.
kept.correction: The Russian marker is the documented rule, not the inconsistency. docs\MODES.md:46 prescribes the first line '-- Ядро: без проверок режима (docs/MODES.md)' (or '-- Ядро: …') for Core scripts, and 61 coop_*.script follow it. The real inconsistency is the Core files without it: coop_pda_marks_local ('-- Core: ...'), coop_trader_reputation, coop_item_entity_state, and coop_loot_claim (a --[[ block). Switching to an English form means changing MODES.md first. The work tags used as descriptions ('Dev 57 G9-2.' credit_events 2, 'Dev 57 G9-3.' credit_loot 2, 'R32 W8:' item_entity_state 1) are valid findings. check_layers.py blanks comments, so it does not check the marker (confirmed).

kept.title: coop_menu.script (2403 lines) and coop_debug_ui.script (2343) each mix several jobs
kept.detail: In coop_menu one class does window building (470-966), the map (1281-1542), the timeline (1542-1706), per-frame animation (1708-1766), session status (1769-1868) and session control: host, connect, disconnect, nick and port checks (2037-2324). In coop_debug_ui the catalogs and their data (280-468), the catalog pages (1050-1436), the action pages (1436-1618), the feed, the popover and the window plumbing all sit in one file.
kept.fix: Split coop_menu into coop_menu (window, building, animation), coop_menu_map (map + route + timeline) and coop_menu_session (status texts, host/connect/disconnect, storage). Split coop_debug_ui catalogs and pages into coop_debug_ui_catalog.script. No behaviour change.

kept.title: coop_economy_mdata (1889 lines) holds five subsystems
kept.detail: It holds se vars (around 300-620), item riders (section '2.', 623-791), per-player m_data (section '3.', 795-1250), world keys (1255-1360), the clone transactions and the bolts handoff (1400-1760). Each has its own queues, stats and polls joined in one actor_on_update (1777-1832).
kept.fix: Split into coop_economy_mdata_se / _items / _player / _world (plus clone) behind the same public functions. Keep one update dispatcher.

kept.title: Adapter for Tactical Compass, a mod that is off in the G.A.M.M.A profile
kept.detail: The header (4-5) says Tactical Compass is 'off in the G.A.M.M.A profile', and docs/MOD_REPLACEMENTS.md:33 lists it as 'GAMMA, выкл в профиле'. The owner's rule (TZ Р22, CLAUDE.md) says disabled mods are not work. Still there: 227 lines of coop_hud_tc (it wraps tc_utils.get_world_coordinates and tc_markers.drop_stale_spots, polls at 4 Hz) plus the tc_binder hook in coop_hud_markers 714-716. It is also named coop_hud_* instead of coop_mods_*.
kept.fix: Remove coop_hud_tc.script and the tc_binder branch, and update MOD_REPLACEMENTS.md. If it must stay, rename it coop_mods_tactical_compass and say why.
kept.correction: This is not dead code but a deliberate, documented option. docs\MOD_REPLACEMENTS.md:33 says Tactical Compass is off in the profile, but if a player turns it on and switches our compass off, allies and pings go into it (coop_hud_tc header 4-17). Dropping it is an owner decision under the 'disabled mods are not work' rule, and behaviour_change true is right. The tc_binder branch in coop_hud_markers 714-716 feeds the markers' own PDA sweep (on_tc_spot 574-578) when TC holds the engine callback, so it goes or stays with TC support as a whole. If it stays, the valid part is naming: it should be coop_mods_tactical_compass, not coop_hud_*. Kind should be wrong_place/naming, not dead.

kept.title: The player-slot limit 16 is hard-coded twice with different explanations
kept.detail: core_hud 53 has MAX_PLAYER_SLOT = 16 '-- coop_protocol.h kMaxPlayers'. economy_core 281-282 has player_id = int(v, 0, 16) 'coop_protocol.h kMaxPeerSlots'. The engine has kMaxPlayers = 16 and kMaxPeerSlots = kMaxPlayers + 1 (engine/src/xrCoop/coop_protocol.h:127,133). The numbers are right, but they are two copies and one comment names the wrong constant.
kept.fix: Define one Lua constant (for example coop_economy_core.MAX_PEER = 16, the last slot id), or read it from coop.session_info(), and use it in both places.
kept.correction: The duplicate is real, but the economy_core location is wrong: it is coop_economy_core.script:362-363 (player_id = int(v, 0, 16), comment 'kMaxPeerSlots'), not 281-282. core_hud 53 (MAX_PLAYER_SLOT = 16, used at 186 as an inclusive peer-id bound) names kMaxPlayers, while the bound it means is kMaxPeerSlots - 1 (coop_protocol.h:127, 133). Both values are right.

kept.title: Adding a favourite past 200 may drop the one just added
kept.detail: toggle_fav (265-276) sets the key, sorts all keys, then trims with 'while #list > 200 do table.remove(list) end', which removes the alphabetically last entries. If the new key sorts last it is removed at once, and the function returns false: the star click does nothing.
kept.fix: Trim before inserting (refuse at 200, or drop the oldest by insertion order), never the key being added.

kept.title: Marker sources allocate twice per marker per refresh
kept.detail: src_allies (314-333) builds a color table { A.color(...) } per ally every 100 ms. normalize (197-218) then copies it into another color table, copies the position through copy_pos, which makes a pcall closure per marker (160), and builds the key string. src_pings (470-479) and the transition source do the same. That is 10 Hz, not per frame, so the payoff is small.
kept.fix: Let sources return colour components (r, g, b) or a shared palette table. Make copy_pos read p.x/p.y/p.z without the closure when p is a plain table.

refuted.why: Not a hot path. Stock main_hud_shown (_g.script:301-313 in temp\anomaly_unpack) is about seven field reads, one Check_UI and one console read, called about five times per frame. The duplicate hud_visible helpers are already part of finding 4. The per-tick cache adds a staleness risk: start_hold runs from on_key_press for kUSE (transition 972-985, arena 612-629), and the same press can open a talk dialog within the same time_global tick, so a cached 'visible' could outlive it for a frame.

Already handled. The pda_sweep is on the known FPS-audit list, and the vault note 'FPS — аудит update и AI Lua — 2026-11-10.md' line 35 records 0.051 ms of a 0.205 ms HUD with the conclusion 'оптимизировать незачем' (not worth optimizing). The fix also changes behaviour: only the compass calls list() (compass 1108-1109), and the compass skips it while hidden, so the sweep would pause during the PDA or inventory. On resume the 'about 32 frames' refill holds only if pda.first is reset, which brings back the 2048-ids-per-frame spike (SCAN_FIRST 104, MAX_ID 65534). Otherwise the refill takes about 683 frames.

The premise is wrong. CSE_Abstract::spawn_ini() caches its CInifile in m_ini_file and builds it only once (engine\src\xrServerEntities\xrServer_Object_Base.cpp:182-192), so key_of (coop_trader_reputation.script:25-38) does not reparse the ini each second. refresh runs at 1 Hz, only on the decider (41), over a handful of players: not a hot path. Caching keys by avatar id would add staleness when ids are reused.

hotpaths-measure.summary: Ни одна из находок ниже не измерена. Я проверил, что эти места кода действительно выполняются каждый кадр или для каждого NPC и объекта, но сколько миллисекунд они стоят, пока не знаю. Единственный замер на стенде (13.11) показал: кадр клиента 13–15 мс, из них около 11 мс рендер, а «планировщик» скачет от 5 до 18 мс. Скрипты HUD стоят всего 0,2 мс, поэтому трогать их незачем. Весь наш Lua (128 обработчиков actor_on_update в 112 файлах и наши обёртки вокруг каждого колбэка GAMMA) работает внутри этого «планировщика». Скорее всего, самое дорогое место — coop_mods_item_state: каждый кадр он обходит весь инвентарь игрока и на каждый предмет делает десятки обращений к движку, хотя меняться могут только оружие с заклиниванием или камуфляжем. Второе — вопросы о роли процесса (coop_mode.leads_here и подобные, около 1100 мест в коде): каждый такой вопрос заново выбирает слой режима, это около 7 pcall и 5 вызовов движка. Причём такие вопросы задаются в путях, которые работают для каждого NPC. Третье — маршрутизатор колбэков: на каждый вызов любого обработчика любого мода он делает два обращения к движку под замком, хотя для доменов owner и view ответ всегда «да». Дальше идут: обёртка GAMMA get_visible_value, которая на хосте при каждой оценке видимости создаёт две таблицы и замыкание; самые частые проверки is_active, is_client, is_live, привязанные через медленный luabind; coop.players() и Session::peers(), которые каждый кадр копируют список игроков вместе со строками; выделения памяти в снимках NPC 15 раз в секунду. Ещё найден один баг: при больших очередях звуковые Lua-события сверх 32 за кадр молча теряются. Все предложенные исправления не меняют того, что видит, слышит и чувствует игрок; исключение — только этот баг. План замера: собрать конфигурацию ProfiledDX11 с Optick, расставить около 40 зон PROF_EVENT в коде кооператива (сейчас там нет ни одной), добавить включаемый по команде замер Lua по обработчикам и счётчики вызовов, плюс таймеры CStatTimer, которые работают и в обычной Release-сборке. Каждый режим меряется отдельно: в Коопе хост и клиенты, в Сервере сервер мира, сервер карты и клиент. Только после этого оптимизировать, начиная с первых 10 мест по измеренным миллисекундам.

kept.title: Rider capture walks the whole actor inventory every frame with dozens of engine calls per item
kept.detail: update() is registered on actor_on_update with no interval (:1390 `function() step("update", update) end`) and ends with capture_inventory() (:1144). capture_inventory (:1100-1106) runs db.actor:iterate_inventory with a fresh closure; per item it calls observe(id) (:319-334: fresh() -> coop.released_after, instance() :59-65 -> data() + alife_object(id):name(), data() again) and capture(s,id) for both specs (:1041-1061). Each capture first evaluates C().active() (luabind), owns(id) (:336-338 -> coop_mode.actor_is_player(), which re-resolves the mode layer, see the coop_mode finding, + coop_mods_core.root_of :332-340 = alife() + sim:object per parent level + db.actor:id()), then instance() again, live(s) (:43-54: for the camo spec it CALLS the GAMMA mod's save_state(snapshot) and allocates `snapshot` per item), data(). Only then does it return for the vast majority of items that have no rider (:1048-1050). Estimate: ~40-50 Lua->engine/pcall transitions per item per frame; a GAMMA inventory of 80-150 items gives thousands per frame on every playing machine (Coop host + clients, Server players; ghosts return at :1101). update() also allocates parts_dirty = {} every frame (:1129) and on the world server watch_routes (:532-546) builds coop.players() and a new table every frame. Runs inside the engine 'scheduler' timer (4.9-18 ms on the 2026-11-13 stand).
kept.fix: Behaviour-identical rewrite of the per-frame scan: (1) compute once per frame m=data(), tbl[s]=live(s) per spec, active, actor_is_player, actor id; items from db.actor:iterate_inventory are the actor's, so owns()/root_of is not needed for them; (2) capture can only act on ids in keys(live table) or keys(m[s.key]) (capture is a no-op otherwise, :1048-1050), so iterate those small tables and check ownership, instead of the whole inventory; run observe() for ids that have a record or a seen[] stamp; (3) reuse the parts_dirty table (swap two tables). Keep the same frame of capture (the comment at :1058-1059 needs it in the action's frame). Measure with a profile_timer around capture_inventory first.
kept.correction: The cost is real: capture_inventory runs every frame (coop_mods_item_state.script:1100-1107, registered at :1390). capture() is called per item per spec and checks owns() (actor_is_player + root_of) before it can return (:1041-1050), and live() runs camo save_state into a fresh table (:43-54). Step (2) of the fix is wrong for observe(), though. observe() must keep running for every inventory item. On first sight of an id (seen[id]==nil) it calls restore(), which calls restore_se() (:303-316, :332). That applies SE-saved rider state and records the seen stamp; it also catches an instance change for an id that already has one. Running observe only for ids with a record or a seen stamp would skip restore_se for items reached only by this scan, which changes behaviour. The safe narrowing is to the capture half alone: per frame, take the union of keys of live(s) and m[s.key], check ownership there, and hoist data(), live(s), active and actor_is_player out of the item loop. Also, watch_routes only reaches coop.players() on the world server: in co-op the bridge hook is nil (:534-535).

kept.title: Every role question re-selects the mode layer: ~7 pcalls and 5 engine calls, ~1100 call sites, no memo
kept.detail: ask() (:195-202) calls current() (:178-192), which pcalls each installed layer's applies() until one says yes, then pcalls layer[k]. In a co-op session hostplay.applies (coop_hostplay_mode.script:37-39) = engine("is_active") (luabind, via pcall in call()) + server_mode() (:~27: is_map_server, is_dedicated, levels.split, each pcalled); then decides_world/leads_here = host() -> engine("is_host") (another pcall + luabind). Single player falls through hostplay and srv.applies (coop_srv_mode.script:53-59) to NONE. hostplay where()/decider() call row(peer) (:50-57) which builds the whole coop.players() table per question. Call sites in coop_*.script: decides_world 320, leads_here 246, actor_is_player 193, is_player_mirror 144, writes 118, where 68, decider 19; several sit in per-NPC paths (coop_mods_nta.script:420/474, coop_npc_world.script:760-764, coop_npc_compat.script:1148-1150 get_visible_value) and per inventory item (coop_mods_item_state.script:337).
kept.fix: Memoize current() and the plain answers (actor_is_player, decides_world, leads_here, is_player_mirror) until the mode can change: best an engine raw-C `coop.mode_epoch()` bumped on every session/phase/mode change (and on Lua-initiated host/disconnect), else a per-frame key (one time_global read per frame); drop the memo in install()/uninstall(). hostplay row(): use a per-frame cached roster (see players() finding). Same answers, far fewer calls.

kept.title: Callback router: every call of every mod's handler pays two engine calls and a lock, even where it always runs
kept.detail: guard() (:196-214) wraps every RegisterScriptCallback/AddUniqueCall/CreateTimeEvent handler of every mod (GAMMA included: npc_on_update, monster_on_update, squad_on_update, smart_terrain_on_update per object on the host, ~all actor_on_update). Per call: runs(d) (coop_router.cpp:490-498, parse_domain) + note(d,"ran") (coop_router.cpp:501-514: two string parses + xrCriticalSectionGuard g_lock + counters); on a client also pcall + vararg finish(). routes::runs_here (xrCoop/coop_routes.h:789-799) returns true for Owner and View unconditionally, so runs() is a constant for them (coop_* = view, actor_* = owner by default, configs/coop_route.ltx). Skips (client, host-domain actor_on_update every frame) add note_skip: two std::map<string> finds under the lock (coop_routes.h:983-1000). Our own 128 actor_on_update registrations in 112 files go through it every frame too.
kept.fix: Specialize at wrap time (domain is fixed per wrapper): owner/view -> no runs() call; count 'ran' in a Lua integer per domain and hand the totals to the engine once per second or when coop_status asks (one note call with a count; small API addition). host/level/none -> read a domain-runs bitmask the engine pushes on session/mode change (or the epoch memo above); keep skip counts per wrapper in Lua (origin[w] already holds script/callback) and flush periodically. Keep the wrapper frame on the stack (R32 W2a scope rule) and the client pcall. Status counters lag by at most 1 s; game behaviour unchanged.

kept.title: The five most-called predicates (is_active, is_host, is_client, is_live, self_id) are luabind-bound; the rest of coop.* is raw C
kept.detail: script_register (:2373-2385) binds l_is_active/l_is_host/l_is_client/l_is_live/l_self_id (:709-721, no arguments) through luabind def(); every other coop function is a lua_CFunction (register_raw). These five sit under every helper active()/live() in coop_mods_core.script:95-97, coop_quests_core.script:35-39, coop_npc_players.script:70-74, coop_economy_core.script:82, under coop_mode's applies()/host(), and coop_client_binders.script:66-68 on_client() which runs per binder method call on a client. Lua call sites: api.is_active 98, api.is_live 28, api.is_client 21, api.self_id 16, api.is_host 10 (+ coop.* forms).
kept.fix: Register the five as raw lua_CFunction (lua_pushboolean/lua_pushnumber, same names, same results) in register_raw and remove the luabind module block. No arguments, so the 'wrong overload is fatal' reason for raw C applies equally. Microbenchmark luabind vs raw on the stand to size the win.

kept.title: get_visible_value wrapper allocates two tables and a closure and walks debug upvalues on every visibility evaluation
kept.detail: The engine calls the Lua functor visual_memory_manager.get_visible_value for each visible object of each NPC on every visibility update (engine/src/xrGame/visual_memory_manager.cpp:360-371, called at :460 and :471). The coop wrapper (:1146-1170), in a session where leads_here, does for EVERY call (NPC targets included): C.active() + coop_mode.leads_here() (layer re-selection), P.peer_of(id), `values, saved = {...}, {}` (2 tables), 3x debug.getupvalue/setupvalue, rawset of a NEW IsMoveState closure, pcall(old...), then restore() with 3 more setupvalue calls. For player targets also coop_mode.where(peer) -> hostplay row() -> coop.players() table build. This is the hottest Lua entry on a host with many NPCs.
kept.fix: Behaviour-identical: module-level reusable `values`/`saved` arrays; one IsMoveState closure created once that reads a module-level `cur_move` (save/restore it around the call for reentrancy); role answers from the memo; frame-cached roster for where(). Optional second step after reading GAMMA's formula on the stand: if jacketmult/get_camo_k/pewpewmult are used only for the actor target, call `old` directly for non-player targets. Time it first (Optick zone around the functor call at visual_memory_manager.cpp:370 + Lua counter).

kept.title: Measurement step 1: build ProfiledDX11 (Optick) next to the release build
kept.detail: The solution has ProfiledDX11|x64 (:281) and builds the optick project in it (:261, :1244-1245). ProfiledDX11 defines XRCORE_PROFILER for xrGame, xrCore, xrEngine and xrRender_R4 (vcxproj PreprocessorDefinitions), so profiler.h switches PROF_* to Optick; Release-AVX does not. Output goes to engine/_build/_game/bin_dbg/AnomalyDX11.exe (Common.props:13,20; xrEngine.vcxproj:248-249), separate from the release bin. The frame marker exists (xrEngine/device.cpp:361 PROF_FRAME). Differences to keep in mind: ProfiledDX11 xrGame has EnableEnhancedInstructionSet NotSet (no AVX) and WholeProgramOptimization false, so compare shares and per-zone deltas, not absolute ms against Release-AVX. temp/build_guarded_fast.ps1:17 builds DX11-AVX only.
kept.fix: When the owner's game is closed: msbuild engine-vs2022.sln -p:Configuration=ProfiledDX11 -p:Platform=x64 (same guarded wrapper, separate log). Copy the bin_dbg binaries into a copy of the stand's bin (never game/, mo2/ or E:/Programs/RayLink), keep the stand's release binaries aside. Get the Optick GUI of the optick-git version (a download: owner's OK) and attach over TCP to the running exe; capture 10-20 s windows.
kept.correction: The configuration facts hold. ProfiledDX11 is in the solution (engine-vs2022.sln:281); optick is built in it (:1244-1245); XRCORE_PROFILER is defined in the ProfiledDX11 groups of xrGame (vcxproj:205), xrCore (:185), xrEngine (:439) and xrRender_R4 (:184), but not in Release-AVX (xrGame.vcxproj:390-415); ProfiledDX11 has no AVX and no whole-program optimisation. The build steps are wrong, though. (1) The guarded wrapper builds engine-ci/src/engine-vs2022.sln with -p:Configuration=DX11-AVX hardcoded and checks AnomalyDX11AVX.exe (temp/build_guarded_fast.ps1:11,14,17), so 'same guarded wrapper' cannot build ProfiledDX11 without a parameter. (2) The output is not separate from the release build: Common.props:20 sets OutDir bin_dbg for every configuration. xrEngine only changes the exe name (AnomalyDX11 vs AnomalyDX11AVX, xrEngine.vcxproj:248-249 vs :278-279), and xrCore has no per-config OutDir or TargetName, so a ProfiledDX11 build in the same tree overwrites the release xrCore.dll in bin_dbg. xrGame alone gets bin_dbg/x64/<Config>. Build in the engine tree, not engine-ci, or give the build its own OutDir, and copy the release binaries aside first.

kept.title: Measurement step 2: PROF_EVENT zones for our engine code (there are none in xrGame/coop or xrCoop today)
kept.detail: grep finds no PROF_EVENT/START_PROFILE in xrGame/coop or xrCoop. Stock zones already exist around us: CGamePersistent::OnFrame (GamePersistent.cpp:700, contains coop::on_frame :701), CScriptBinder::shedule_Update (script_binder.cpp:285, includes the actor binder = all actor_on_update handlers), CAI_Stalker::UpdateCL (ai_stalker.cpp:1025). Zones to add (compile to nothing outside ProfiledDX11): Z1 coop::on_frame (coop_manager.cpp:846); Z2 inside Manager::frame (:757-791): network pump m_world.update/m_session.update, join::frame, sync::frame, health_ledger::frame; Z3 first line of each pass called from sync::frame (:236-300, ~30 one-liners: viewers, players, player_touch, survival, checkpoints, death, rest, autosave, presence incl. sound::frame/build_tags, items, entities incl. host_send_snapshots/host_process_events/watch_decider, events, reconcile_frame, objects incl. host_stream/client_scan/client_apply_bodies, the 4 vehicles passes, requests, dialog, trade, money, worldstate, script::frame with deliver_chat/inbox/engine/lost, syncapi, story, progress, mode().frame, monster_fx, debug); Z4 per object: coop::remote::update_cl (coop_remote.cpp:261), entities::drive_mirror (coop_entities.cpp:2613), players::drive_avatar; Z5 engine->Lua entries: sound::lua_frame (coop_sound.cpp:763), script deliver_* ; Z6 the stock Lua functor calls our wrappers hide in: visual_memory_manager.cpp:370 and ai_stalker.cpp:1156-1159. Do NOT zone l_runs/l_note/l_scope/is_remote_creature/binder_action: called thousands of times a frame, the zone cost would swamp them; measure those by counts x microbenchmark (step 3).
kept.fix: Add the zones as single PROF_EVENT("coop ...") lines with static names (not PROF_EVENT_DYNAMIC, see the profiler.h finding). One commit, no logic change; Release-AVX unaffected (macros empty).

kept.title: Measurement step 3: Lua-side timing per handler, per role question and per hot wrapper (opt-in, zero cost when off)
kept.detail: profile_timer exists (engine/src/xrServerEntities/script_engine_script.cpp:127-190, rdtsc via CPU::GetCLK, recursion-safe) and coop_hud_markers already uses it (perf_start/perf_stop :651-674, printed by coop_status). Nothing times the router or the other hot Lua. Optick has dynamic push/pop (3rd party/optick-git/src/optick.h:658-660 Event::Push(const char*)/Pop) usable from a raw C function in the profiled build.
kept.fix: (a) In coop_route.guard: when a module flag is on (set by a debug console command, read as one upvalue test per call), time each call by (callback, script) with profile_timer, or in ProfiledDX11 call raw C coop.prof_push(label)/coop.prof_pop() (label precomputed at wrap time) so every handler, GAMMA's included, appears as its own zone under CScriptBinder::shedule_Update. Print top-20 by ms/s and the empty-handler wrapper cost. (b) Counters per second: coop_mode ask() by key; coop.players() calls; items visited by item_state per frame; get_visible_value wrapper calls; CreateTimeEvent/AddUniqueCall registrations. Route call totals per domain already exist (coop.route.note, coop_status). (c) Targeted timers: item_state capture_inventory, get_visible_value wrapper, coop_npc_disguise npc_on_update. (d) Microbenchmarks (stand-only console command, 100k iterations): wrapped vs direct empty handler, coop_mode.leads_here(), api.is_active() luabind vs a raw C getter, time_global(), coop.players(). Per-call ns x counters/s = ms/s for each hotspot. (e) GC: collectgarbage('count') delta per 10 s.

kept.title: Measurement step 4: coop CStatTimers in the release build, printed by coop_mapserver_stats
kept.detail: CStatTimer::Begin/End return at once unless stats are on (xrCore/FTimer.h:208-219, g_bEnableStatGather = rs_stats). coop_mapserver_stats already prints a 'frame parts' line from Device.Statistic (:143-151), and the stand harness switches rs_stats on and logs it every 10 s (temp/stand/coop_zz_perf.script, auto_world.ps1 -Perf). Our whole on_frame is only inside the stock 'engine' total today.
kept.fix: Add a coop-owned array of CStatTimer (coop frame total, net pump, entities/snapshots, objects, presence+sound, script delivery, the rest of sync::frame) with FrameStart/FrameEnd in coop::on_frame, and append them to the frame-parts line. Gives a continuous ms figure on Release-AVX (no Optick build needed) to confirm each optimisation on the normal stand runs.

kept.title: Measurement step 5: protocol per mode, and the top-10 list to prove before any optimisation
kept.detail: Existing harness: -Perf copies coop_zz_perf.script, starts rs_stats, logs coop_mapserver_stats every 10 s and coop_status every 30 s (:73-75, :123-125). The only frame data so far (vault, 2026-11-13, client 1280x720): frame 12.8-14.8 ms, render 10.5-11.8, scheduler 4.9-18 (jumpy), HUD scripts 0.205 ms total. No host or server-mode numbers.
kept.fix: Per CLAUDE.md, separately per mode: Coop = host + 2 clients; Server = world server + one map server + one client. Same save, a crowded spot (many NPCs), 20 s warm-up, 150 s window, 3 runs, ProfiledDX11 captures plus step 3/4 numbers. Hypotheses to prove or kill, in order: (1) item_state inventory capture, (2) coop_mode role questions, (3) route wrapper overhead, (4) get_visible_value wrapper (host), (5) luabind predicates volume, (6) players()/peers() copies, (7) per-NPC Lua handlers (disguise, nta mirage, silent-kill corpse alert), (8) snapshot/stream allocations at 15 Hz (host/map server), (9) client binder routing + client binder guard, (10) CreateTimeEvent scope walk. Output a table of measured ms per frame and calls/s; optimise only what measures above ~0.1 ms/frame or causes spikes, re-run the same protocol after each change, and check behaviour with tests + a stand scenario per mode.

kept.title: coop.players() copies the session roster twice and builds a table per player on every call; Lua has 4 copies of the wrapper and no frame cache
kept.detail: l_players (:778-832) calls host_seat_plays() (:733-737 -> roster::host_plays_in(peers())) = copy #1, then iterates mgr().session().peers() = copy #2. Session::peers() (xrCoop/coop_session.cpp:2315-2330) returns std::vector<PeerInfo> by value; PeerInfo holds std::string nick and address (xrCoop/coop_session.h:55-67, 'ip:port' exceeds SSO). Then one Lua table with ~10 fields per player. Lua wrappers that call it per question: coop_npc_players.script:107, coop_mods_core.script:248, coop_quests_core.script:53 (identical), coop_economy_core.script:268 (copying) and :303 others_count, hostplay row() (coop_hostplay_mode.script:50). Per-frame callers: coop_srv_progress.script:145 and :411, coop_mods_item_state.script:537, plus every coop_mode.where/decider in co-op mode.
kept.fix: One frame-cached roster in one module (coop_npc_players already caches others/everyone per frame at :151-173: add the roster there, document 'read-only, valid this frame'), the other modules call it. Engine: give Session a const view or for_each_peer visitor so l_players/host_seat_plays do not copy.
kept.correction: The cost is real (coop_script.cpp:778-832; peers() by value, coop_session.cpp:2315-2330). Two details are wrong. 'Copy #1' happens only on a machine that does not decide the world: host_seat_plays returns mode().actor_is_player() on the decider without touching peers() (:733-737). So the co-op host and the world server copy once per call; a client copies twice. And watch_routes (coop_mods_item_state.script:537) is not a per-frame caller in co-op: it returns at :535, because hostplay's hook is nil. A shared frame-cached roster is only safe if no caller mutates the returned rows or list. The Lua wrappers today hand each caller its own table (coop_npc_players.script:107-110, coop_mods_core.script:248-251, coop_quests_core.script:53-56, coop_economy_core.script:268+), so callers must be audited before the risk is called low.

kept.title: Session::peers() vector copies (with strings) in several every-frame engine passes
kept.detail: Every frame on the host: worldstate host_join_frame (:433) and level_join_frame (:490) copy peers(); sound host_frame (coop_sound.cpp:290-293) builds a new targets vector plus a peers() copy; checkpoints host_frame (coop_checkpoints.cpp:476-477) builds a new xr_set<u16> plus a peers() copy; survival::frame (coop_survival.cpp:3209-3210) and presence build_tags (coop_presence.cpp:769-770) build a new xr_vector<PlayerRef> with nick strings via collect_players (:2884-2928, peers() copy on the host). Also story ghost_frame (coop_story.cpp:1996) while relations are pending and vehicles decider_frame (coop_vehicles_state.cpp:286). The allocator zero-fills every block (vault 2026-11-13), so small allocations are not free.
kept.fix: Session::for_each_peer(F) (or a const reference with the main-thread contract) for these loops; static/member scratch vectors cleared per frame (capacity kept) for targets, PlayerRef lists and the checkpoint set.

kept.title: Sound Lua events beyond 32 in a frame are dropped silently, not deferred
kept.detail: lua_frame (:763-787) swaps g_lua into a local `now` (:779, comment: 'a handler may cause new events: they wait for the next frame'), fires at most kLuaPerFrame = 32 (:47, :782-786) and then lets `now` go out of scope: events 33..64 (queue cap kMaxLuaQueue 64, :438-440) are destroyed, not counted in g_st. Those are coop_avatar_step / coop_npc_sound / coop_npc_sound_stop callbacks (:714-716), so in busy frames footstep/NPC-sound listeners miss events (a stop can be lost and a sound left playing). The swap also throws away the vector capacity every frame.
kept.fix: After the budget, move the unprocessed tail back to the front of g_lua (keep it ahead of the new events), or iterate with an index and erase the processed prefix; count real drops. Keep two persistent vectors and swap them to keep capacity.

kept.title: NPC snapshot capture allocates per creature at 15 Hz and scans all level objects
kept.detail: host_send_snapshots (:816-871, every 66 ms, :68) loops over all Level().Objects (:839) with smart_cast, and for every creature creates `Writer entry(128)` (:849, a std::vector reserve = heap alloc + free), capture_attachments (:475-498) returns a State with std::vector<Item> and a std::string bone per attachment (xrCoop/coop_attachments.h:15-19,45), and each flush allocates `Writer out` (:829) to copy the body again. Same pattern in objects host_stream (coop_objects.cpp:2244-2290, `Writer w(32)` per moving body at :2286). Host / map server main thread.
kept.fix: Hoist `entry` out of the loop and entry.clear() per creature (capacity kept); keep a scratch `out`; write attachments straight into the entry (or reserve kMaxItems and a fixed bone buffer); Batcher could expose a reusable entry writer. Optionally keep a creature-id list maintained on spawn/destroy instead of scanning every object. Same bytes on the wire.

kept.title: Disguise npc_on_update: per NPC update x per player, engine lookups and allocations that are the same for the whole frame
kept.detail: npc_on_update (:361-410) runs for every NPC update on the host with clients. Per player: P.object_of_peer(peer) (coop_npc_players.script:213-220: self_peer pcall + pcall(api.avatar_of) + level.object_by_id), proxy:id(), npc:see(proxy), in_disguise_zone(proxy) (:260-266: 2 zones x obj:position() = new vector userdata + zone:inside), and per seen pair game.get_game_time() (new CTime userdata, :383, again :406). Per call also tosox_enabled() (:310-312) and is_companion -> npc:has_info (:314-316).
kept.fix: Build a per-frame table per peer {proxy, id, in_zone} on the first NPC update of the frame (key: time_global(), or reuse coop_npc_players.others(), which is already frame-cached); read the proxy position once; read the game time once per call. Same results within the frame.

kept.title: Per-NPC handlers ask the role before their cheap check
kept.detail: sample_mirage (:419-420), run from an npc_on_update handler for every NPC (:482-484), evaluates C().active() and coop_mode.leads_here() before mi.is_mirage(npc); the npc_on_choose_weapon wrapper does the same (:473-474). The silent-kill npc_on_update replacement (coop_npc_world.script:760-765) asks P.active() and coop_mode.leads_here() on every NPC update before pcall(corpse_alert).
kept.fix: Test mi.is_mirage(npc) first (confirm on the stand that it is a pure predicate); with the role memo the remaining questions are cheap. Same outcome.

kept.title: Client binder routing takes the router lock twice per binder method call
kept.detail: CScriptBinder::shedule_Update and the other binder methods go through call_routed (script_binder.cpp:88-92, Update at :291) -> binder_action (:737-750). On a mirror it calls load_overrides() (:621-625, takes g_lock even when already loaded), takes g_lock again and looks the slot up by pointer (binder_slot :567-588). That is every non-puppet object's binder update on a client (items, physics, doors, lights, anomalies). The 15 guarded binder classes add coop_client_binders.script:143-150: api.is_client() (luabind) + pcall per call.
kept.fix: Make g.loaded an atomic checked before locking; cache the resolved slot index (plus a generation bumped by load_overrides) in CScriptBinder so the per-update path is lock-free; raw is_client (luabind finding). Same actions.

kept.title: coop.route.scope() builds script-key strings it throws away, on every CreateTimeEvent/AddUniqueCall
kept.detail: wrap_time_event and wrap_unique (coop_route.script:375-399) call scope_now() -> l_scope (:553-561) on every registration. l_scope uses stack_facts (:130-178), which walks up to 64 frames and, until it meets a non-helper script, builds routes::script_key(ar.source) as std::string per frame; l_scope reads only f.domain. GAMMA mods create time events often (some every frame).
kept.fix: A domain-only stack walk for l_scope: lua_getstack + lua_getinfo("f") + registry lookup, no source parsing, stop at the first registered wrapper. Count registrations per second first (step 3) to size it.

kept.title: 128 actor_on_update registrations, ~100 of them a private 250-1000 ms timer
kept.detail: 128 RegisterScriptCallback("actor_on_update") in 112 coop scripts, 9 unregister sites. Most start with their own gate (e.g. coop_arena.script:2108-2112, coop_core_chat.script:609-612, coop_npc_combat/companions/disguise/logic/meet/world at 250 ms, coop_npc_relations 1000 ms). Each still costs, every frame: the route wrapper (2 engine calls + lock, pcall on a client), a Lua call, and a luabind time_global() (452 time_global() calls in coop scripts; stock binds it via luabind, script_engine_script.cpp:246).
kept.fix: One coop tick service (coop_mods_core or coop_main): every(ms, fn, name) with a due-time list, one actor_on_update, one time_global() per frame, per-tick pcall and error report in one place. Move only pure timers; keep direct registrations for adapters that must run at their place in the dispatch chain relative to GAMMA handlers (changing that order is a behaviour risk). Removes ~100 wrapped calls per frame.
kept.correction: The counts are right (128 registrations in 112 files, 9 unregisters, 452 time_global; the luabind def is at script_engine_script.cpp:246). But 'behaviour_change false' only holds if the tick service keeps each script's route domain. coop_route gives every handler its script's domain, and that domain is also the R32 W2a scope the writer gate reads from the stack (coop_route.script:168-175, 196-215). Most coop_* scripts are view (coop_route.ltx:66), but coop_wipe = host, coop_rest = owner and coop_death = owner (coop_route_f3.ltx:9-11), and all three register actor_on_update. Moving coop_wipe's timer into a view-domain service in coop_mods_core would run it on clients. Keep one service per domain (or exclude the non-view scripts), and keep each script's own wrapper on the stack while its tick runs. coop_arena's handler (coop_arena.script:2108-2109) runs wait_tick before its gate, so it is not a pure timer either.

kept.title: Three every-frame polls for 'did the save table change', one with a closure+pcall per frame
kept.detail: coop_economy_mdata actor_on_update (:1779) calls m_data() (:90-94: new closure + pcall around alife_storage_manager.get_state()) every frame; coop_mods_item_state update (:1125) calls data() (:23-26) every frame and again per inventory item inside instance(); coop_mods_world_views actor_on_update (:400-407) calls bind_world (:20-27 -> alife_storage_manager.get_state()) every frame. Three ways to do one thing.
kept.fix: One helper in coop_mods_core that reads the storage identity once per frame (or on load_state/on_game_load) and exposes storage_epoch(); the three modules compare epochs. No closure per frame.

kept.title: drain_tick allocates a closure and reads actor health every frame, using it only at the window edges
kept.detail: drain_tick (:1074-1087, registered :1091) does pcall(function() return tonumber(db.actor.health) end) every frame, then returns while now - drain.start < DRAIN_MS (:1083). coop_mods_core revive_poll (:769-785) reads db.actor.health every frame as well, and respawn_poll (:804-811) does pcall(api.life_of, 0) every frame when a listener exists.
kept.fix: drain_tick: test the window before reading health and use a module-level getter (same samples are used, same result). revive_poll/respawn_poll: share one health read per frame (or read when the engine's life state changes).

kept.title: Server progress: two actor_on_update handlers rebuild the roster every frame
kept.detail: World server: refresh() (:140-170), run from the handler at :358-366 every frame, looks up coop_mode.hook, allocates `live = {}` and iterates C.players() (engine table build). Map server: update() (:408-427, registered :488) allocates `present = {}` and iterates C.players() with C.peer_of/decider per player every frame. No interval.
kept.fix: Frame-cached roster (players() finding); reuse the present/live tables; in refresh() skip the rebuild when the roster and epoch did not change. Do not add a 250 ms interval without the owner's OK (it would change timing).
kept.correction: The per-frame roster use is right (refresh at coop_srv_progress.script:140-175, run from :358-366; map update() at :408-427, registered at :488). The fix's 'skip the rebuild when the roster and epoch did not change' is wrong. live[] also depends on bridge_of(player.id) (:146), a map-server reassignment that can change while the roster stays the same and that bumps generation (:150-156). Skipping on roster+epoch would miss it. Also, `live` becomes `routes` (:174), so 'reuse the live table' needs a two-table swap. The per-player C.peer_of/decider calls are inside local_character (:401-406).

kept.title: One-shot and fight-the-stock work left on actor_on_update for the whole session
kept.detail: unstuck() calls RemoveTimeEvent("cycle","companion_unstuck") every frame on every machine (:106-110). coop_mods_perks.script:436-441 (`if rebound then return end`), coop_pda_rankings.script:138-140 (install once) and coop_mods_mags.script:563-569 (first-run check) stay registered after their one job. coop_mods_perk_abilities.script:590-602 polls PBA.timed_effects every frame to re-wrap on_end; coop_mods_xchg_3dss.script:367-369 retries three installs every frame.
kept.fix: Unregister after the one-shot (pattern already used at coop_mods_misc.script:126 and coop_progress_check.script:777); remove companion_unstuck once after on_game_load and wrap the stock registrar instead of deleting it every frame; install the PBA guard where the effect is created, or poll at 250 ms. Same behaviour.
kept.correction: Only some of the listed handlers are one-shot. coop_mods_perks (:436-441, a rebound flag) and coop_pda_rankings (:138-140; install() sets state.installed first, :100-101) can unregister after their one job. coop_mods_mags actor_on_update (:563-575) is not one-shot: after the first-run check it calls mirror_flush every frame, so only the check can be split off. coop_mods_perk_abilities update (:652-660) also polls and sweeps on timers, so guard_die is one step inside a live handler. Polling it at 250 ms would let an effect restored by a load end unguarded within that window (the add_timed_effect wrap at :605-611 covers only new effects), so guarding at load is the safe change. coop_mods_xchg_3dss update (:365-371) has ongoing complete_scope/silencer work and retries installs only while a mod is absent (install_silencer returns without setting the flag, :312-321). companion_unstuck: the stock registrar is not in the repo, so 'remove once after load' is unverified. Wrapping the registrar is the safe form.

kept.title: Engine string and info lookups each frame before the interval check
kept.detail: actor_on_update (:332-337) reads level.name() every frame before rf_scan/hint_scan test their 2 s timers (:199-201); hint_scan (:285-288) calls has_alife_info(HINT_SENT) every frame on the Bar. coop_pda_marks_local.script:305-312 reads level.name() every frame before its poll gate.
kept.fix: Test the timers first and read the level name after, or cache the level name on level load. Same results.

kept.title: Per-frame table churn while exchanges are pending
kept.detail: watch_tick (:176-200) allocates `keep` and `due` tables every frame while watches exist; deferred_tick (:322-333) allocates a new awaiting_gone table every frame while jobs wait. Called every frame from actor_on_update (:575-580).
kept.fix: Compact the arrays in place (two-index walk) instead of rebuilding them. Same order and outcome.
kept.correction: The allocations are real (coop_mods_xchg.script:176-207, :322-333, called from :575-580). But 'compact in place, same order and outcome' is not true for deferred_tick. It swaps awaiting_gone to a new table before calling job.finish (:324-326) so that finish can queue new jobs. Today a job queued during the walk lands between the kept jobs in walk order; in-place compaction would put it after all kept jobs, which changes completion order in later frames. Use two persistent tables swapped and cleared to keep the exact semantics. watch_tick can compact watches in place, since no callbacks run before `watches = keep` (:207); due callbacks then append to the new watches.

kept.title: Per-creature puppet test recomputed several times a frame; avatar section compared by strcmp
kept.detail: is_remote_driven (:383-399) is reached through coop::remote::is_remote_creature (coop_remote.cpp:241-246) from CustomMonster.cpp:341 and :478 (update_cl, then apply() again at coop_remote.cpp:280), ai_stalker.cpp:1029, 1126, 1664 and base_monster.cpp:350, 380: per creature per frame several evaluations of smart_cast<CActor>, xr_strcmp(cNameSect(), "coop_player_avatar") (:390), is_player_proxy map lookup, is_mirrored. world::is_player_character already compares the docked shared_str (coop_world.cpp:25-28,77); the literal is repeated in coop_join.cpp:106, coop_story.cpp:53, coop_world.cpp:40. g_puppets is looked up 3 times in update_cl/apply (coop_remote.cpp:268, 292, 321).
kept.fix: Use world::is_player_character (pointer compare) in is_remote_driven; one avatar_section() for all four places; decide 'remote creature' once per object on spawn and on session/mode change (a flag in the puppet book), read the flag in the hot paths; one g_puppets lookup per apply.
kept.correction: The repetition is real: is_remote_creature is checked in update_cl and again in apply (coop_remote.cpp:266, 280), and at CustomMonster.cpp:341, ai_stalker.cpp:1029/1126/1664 and base_monster.cpp:350/380. The strcmp is at coop_sync.cpp:390, while world::is_player_character compares the docked shared_str (coop_world.cpp:24-28, 75-77). Two details are wrong. g_puppets.count at :268 is on the not-remote branch, so a puppet's frame does 2 lookups (:292, :321), not 3. And the cached 'remote creature' flag must also be invalidated when a proxy registers or the mirrored set changes, not only on spawn/session/mode change. update_cl explicitly handles 'became remote-driven after it spawned (e.g. proxy registered later)' (:273-274), and is_mirrored/is_player_proxy are per-id runtime state (coop_sync.cpp:395-398). Otherwise a stale flag changes who drives a creature.

kept.title: PROF_EVENT_DYNAMIC re-creates its Optick description on every call
kept.detail: The macro declares `static ::Optick::EventDescription* d = nullptr;` and then assigns `d = ::Optick::CreateDescription(...)` unconditionally (:20-22), so in ProfiledDX11 every pass pays a description creation. That inflates measured costs wherever it is used.
kept.fix: Initialise once (`static auto* d = ::Optick::CreateDescription(...)`) or avoid the macro in hot zones; use PROF_EVENT with static names for the coop zones.
kept.correction: The macro defect is real: profiler.h:21-23 assigns CreateDescription on every pass, unlike Optick's own OPTICK_EVENT, which checks for nullptr first (optick.h:836-838). But PROF_EVENT_DYNAMIC is not used anywhere: the only match outside 3rd party is its definition in xrCore/profiler.h. So it inflates nothing that would be measured today. Treat it as a dead or incorrect macro to fix or delete (one style per thing). Nothing needs to change for the measurement plan beyond using PROF_EVENT.

kept.title: Name tags rebuild their player list and strings every frame
kept.detail: build_tags (:763-806) runs every frame while live: new xr_vector<PlayerRef> with nick copies (collect_players, coop_survival.cpp:2884-2928), Tag with two xr_string (nick, line; :153-162) per visible player, player_rgb per player. survival::frame (coop_survival.cpp:3209-3213) builds the same kind of list every frame for avatar_pose_override.
kept.fix: Static scratch vector (clear() keeps capacity), Tag::nick as a pointer into the roster for the frame, and one collect_players per frame shared by survival and presence.

tools-tests.summary: Тесты в целом есть и покрывают много, но гоняются медленно, и часть из них устроена так, что пропускает ошибки. Почти весь 21-минутный прогон Python съедает test_gates.py. В нём 276 тестов, отдельно он шёл 25:43 (лог temp/g8). Каждый тест заново создаёт два git-репозитория и копирует стенд: один вызов git стоит около 58 мс, запуск PowerShell около 1 с. Нативная сборка тестов — один однопоточный вызов cl на 183 файла без /MP и без предкомпилированного заголовка. 26.11 она компилировалась около 7 минут при 12 ядрах, хотя все 183 файла начинаются с test_util.h, то есть PCH подключается без переделок. Нашла настоящую ошибку в проверке выпуска: check_gates считает штамп Lua-раннера без хеша lua51.lib, а test_lua.cmd его добавляет (проверила: 48 и 40 символов). Поэтому tests.ok выдаётся и раннеру, собранному со старой библиотекой, а тест на это всегда пропускается. Ещё одна ошибка: test_trader_identity_api собирается со старой lua51.lib от 11.11, в которой ещё есть исправленная потом ошибка сборщика мусора LuaJIT. Метка tests.ok не включает 17 Python-тестов, которые гоняют настоящий код движка на заглушках (костёр, контейнеры, торговля, глушитель). Три таких же скрипта в tests/ вообще никто не запускает. Мёртвое и дублированное: деплой и запуск на несуществующие стенды (E:\AnomalyCoop, E:\AnomalyCoopGamma, E:\RayLink2), гибридный сценарий и слой dying для удалённого гибрида, два скрипта-надгробия публикации, сборщик build.sh мимо engine-ci. При этом живой скрипт сборки движка лежит в неотслеживаемой temp/. Ещё 10 одинаковых копий Wait-Log, 21 копия вызова vcvars+cl в Python-тестах (каждый вызов около 4,4 с), 7 копий записи DDS на двух языках. В движке workflow GitHub чужой (ветки апстрима, write-all), compressor с бинарниками нужен только ему, а Optick собирается во всех 16 конфигурациях, хотя в Release-AVX выключен. Ни одна из правок ниже не меняет того, что видит, слышит или чувствует игрок: всё касается только инструментов, тестов и сборки.

kept.title: Native tests: one single-threaded cl over 183 files, full rebuild every run, no PCH
kept.detail: build_tests.cmd:70-77 compiles 4 xrCoop .cpp + "tests\test_*.cpp" (183 files) in ONE cl call without /MP; :52 deletes the exe and every run recompiles everything; ENet (8 C files, :56-63) is recompiled every run too. Evidence from the 26.11 run: temp/tests/obj_enet *.obj 04:41:46-47, test objs from 04:42:05 to 04:49:10, coop_tests.exe 04:49:11, so about 7 minutes of compiling on a 12-CPU machine. All 183 test_*.cpp have test_util.h as their FIRST #include (checked with grep), and test_util.h pulls coop_session.h/coop_protocol.h/coop_wire.h plus <thread>/<functional>/<sstream>, so every TU re-parses the same heavy headers.
kept.fix: Add a tests/test_pch.cpp ('#include "test_util.h"') compiled with /Yc"test_util.h" /Fp, compile the tests with /Yu"test_util.h" /Fp and /MP6 (a cap because the machine is low on memory). Compile ENet only when obj_enet\*.obj is missing. Better: a small tests.vcxproj (MSBuild gives incremental builds with header tracking and /MP), driven by build_tests.cmd.

kept.title: test_gates.py takes most of the 21-minute Python run: fresh git repos, a stand copy and PowerShell per test
kept.detail: temp/g8/pytest_gates_full.txt: '275 passed in 1543.51s (0:25:43)' for this file alone; the whole suite temp/A-S4ME/pytest.log: '803 passed ... in 1268.48s (0:21:08)'. The repos fixture (:120-146) runs git init x2 plus 4 config calls each, add/commit/rev-parse x2 and tag x2 (about 18 git processes; measured 58 ms per git call here). scenario_repo (:1089-1129) also copies all of tools/stand (46 files) plus check_layers.py and friends, creates an engine-ci git worktree and runs ci_sync (:187-199: one `git show` per blob). The file has 21 PowerShell launches (about 1 s each, measured 3146 ms for 3) and stand_head.py subprocesses. pytest-xdist is not installed (checked).
kept.fix: Build both template repos once per session (fixture scope='session': base commit, tags, engine-ci worktree) and give each test a copy with shutil.copytree, or `git clone --local --no-hardlinks` for tests that add commits; create the engine-ci worktree only in the tests that need it. Batch the PowerShell checks into one module-scoped process, as test_stand_patterns.py:126 already does. Install pytest-xdist and run with -n 4. Expected: minutes instead of 20+.
kept.correction: The fixture cost is real. repos (test_gates.py:120-146) costs about 18 git processes per test, and scenario_repo (:1089-1129) is called 21 times; each call copies the 46 tools/stand files plus 7 tools, creates an engine-ci worktree and runs ci_sync with one `git show` per blob. pytest-xdist is not installed. The fix stands. However, the claim that this file is 'most of the 21-minute run' is not shown. temp/g8/pytest_gates_full.txt (19.11, '1 failed, 275 passed in 1543.51s') ran this file alone and took longer than the whole-suite run in temp/A-S4ME/pytest.log (20.11, '1 failed, 803 passed in 1268.48s'). The two runs were a day apart under different load and neither has --durations, so the file's share is unknown. Set payoff to medium until a --durations run measures it.

kept.title: tests.ok gate ignores the lua51.lib part of the Lua runner stamp: a runner linked to a stale LuaJIT passes
kept.detail: test_lua.cmd:67 appends the SHA-1 of LUA51_LIB to the stamp (this was added because a runner linked to an old lib kept the GC barrier bug, test_lua.cmd:10). check_gates.lua_stamp (:755-783) hashes runlua.c, native_coop.cpp, the included headers and test_lua.cmd, but NOT the lib. Verified live: `temp\lua\runlua.exe -stamp` = c80303e5...a6a7dcdfa46e (48 hex), python lua_stamp = c80303e5...a6a7 (40 hex). lua_runner_stale (:794) only checks that the python stamp is a substring of the exe, so a runner built against any lib, the stale one included, passes `--tests-mark write`. Also test_gates.py:3209-3216 (test_lua_stamp_of_this_repository_is_the_runners_when_it_is_fresh) compares with != and therefore always skips ('the shared runner is stale right now').
kept.fix: Keep one implementation of the stamp: check_gates.lua_stamp resolves LUA51_LIB exactly like test_lua.cmd:58-59 and hashes it as the last part, and test_lua.cmd gets it from `python -I tools\check_gates.py --lua-stamp` instead of its own certutil/findstr :hash. lua_runner_stale compares for equality with the string the exe prints for -stamp, not a substring. Change the test to assert instead of skip.

kept.title: The release gate covers only 2 of the 20 native Python slice tests; 3 slice scripts are run by nobody
kept.detail: tests.ok (run_all_tests.cmd) runs N, L, LuaJIT and only tests/tools/test_move_admission_wiring.py (:42). check_gates.py:800-807 runs tests/test_story_worldstate.py on its own, from inside the gate tool. The other 17 tests in tests/tools that compile real engine functions over stubs are run only when someone starts pytest by hand (21 min): campfire_damage, client_ammo_reload, container_reject, trade_delivery, silencer_detach, weapon_clone_wgl, texture_descr_slice and others. No runner names tests/test_s6_hub_paths.py, tests/test_s6_npc_paths.py or tests/test_survival_s6_paths.py: grep of tools/*.cmd|*.py|*.ps1 and docs finds only check_gates.py:802 for test_story_worldstate. A product regression in those engine paths does not block a release.
kept.fix: Turn the 4 tests/test_*.py scripts into pytest tests. Put every engine-slice test (tests/tools slices plus those 4) behind one marker or folder, for example tests/native_slices or -m native. Run that set from run_all_tests.cmd as part of N, and remove native_python_failure from check_gates.py so the gate only reads exit codes. Do the speedups below first so N stays fast.
kept.correction: Corrected counts: there are 21 engine-slice tests, 17 in tests/tools (move_admission_wiring among them) and 4 scripts in tests/. T runs 1 (run_all_tests.cmd:42), and the gate runs 1 (check_gates.py:800-808 runs test_story_worldstate.py). No runner calls the other 16 tests/tools slices or test_s6_hub_paths.py, test_s6_npc_paths.py and test_survival_s6_paths.py. Only release.py:81 mentions pytest, and only as a regex inside the notes checks. Everything else in the finding is correct.

kept.title: 21 copies of the 'write compile.cmd, call vcvars64.bat, run cl' helper; each call costs about 4.4 s
kept.detail: vcvars64 + cl helpers in tests/tools: campfire_damage:46, client_ammo_reload:101, clone_pending_fire:32, clone_placement_hooks:24, container_reject:55, items_gift_late:32, local_zone_release:30, move_admission_wiring:47, proxy_ammo_supply:21, script_relay_slice:42, silencer_detach:18 and :51, texture_descr_slice:55, trader_identity_api:33, trade_delivery:44, weapon_brief_info:42, weapon_clone_wgl:69, world_events_slice:30. In tests/: test_s6_hub_paths.py:72, test_s6_npc_paths.py:64, test_story_worldstate.py:27, test_survival_s6_paths.py:375. Measured: one vcvars64.bat call takes 4399 ms here. test_trader_identity_api.py:33 hardcodes the path and ignores VCVARS. Six files carry an `else: shutil.which("c++")` branch that never runs (Windows only).
kept.fix: conftest.py: a session fixture msvc_env runs `cmd /d /c "call vcvars64.bat && set"` once and parses the environment, plus one helper build_native(sources, includes, out, defines=(), libs=()) that calls cl.exe directly with that environment. Every slice test uses it, and the dead c++ branches go.

kept.title: Runner fixtures with function scope rebuild the same exe for every parameter (15 builds where 3 are enough)
kept.detail: test_campfire_damage.py:26 @pytest.fixture(scope="function") is built for 5 modes (:63). test_weapon_brief_info.py:29 is a plain @pytest.fixture for 3 modes (:61). test_proxy_ammo_supply.py:12 is a plain @pytest.fixture for 7 modes (:38). The source and the binary are identical in every case, so 12 builds are wasted at about 4.4 s vcvars plus cl each.
kept.fix: Use scope='module' with a module-scoped scratch folder (see the scratch-folder finding), as the other slice tests already do (container_reject.py:44, world_events_slice.py:50).

kept.title: The identity API test links the stale engine/_build lua51.lib (11.11, before the LuaJIT GC barrier fix)
kept.detail: Default LUA51_LIB = engine/_build/_game/bin_dbg/x64/Release-AVX/lua51.lib. That file is dated 11.11.2026 01:27, while engine-ci's lib is dated 26.11.2026 04:41. test_lua.cmd:10 notes that an old lib 'kept the LuaJIT GC barrier bug that f8470a3c fixed' and test_credit_events crashed 1 run in 40 because of it. So this test runs Lua on the known-buggy VM and can crash or pass by chance. test_lua.cmd:58-59 resolves the lib differently (engine-ci first), so there are two resolvers.
kept.fix: One LUA51_LIB resolver shared by both. Better: link the lib that test_luajit.cmd builds from the current sources (next finding), so no test depends on an engine build at all.
kept.correction: Default and dates are confirmed: :28 defaults to engine/_build/.../lua51.lib dated 11.11.2026 01:27, while engine-ci's is dated 26.11.2026. However, the 'known-buggy VM, can crash by chance' risk does not apply here. f8470a3c fixed the barrier in lua_setupvalue, and this harness loads scripts with setfenv(loadfile(...)) (:124) without calling setupvalue. The real problems: (1) the test runs a lib older than the current LuaJIT sources, which predates the xr_alloc arena of 2026-11-13; (2) it is a second lib resolver that disagrees with test_lua.cmd:58-59; (3) the vcvars path is hardcoded at :33. Risk low, payoff low.

kept.title: LuaJIT for tests comes from two places: rebuilt from all sources on every run, and borrowed from an MSBuild output
kept.detail: test_luajit.cmd:39-48 compiles every lj_*.c/lib_*.c/xr_alloc.c into lua51_test.lib on every run: no cache, one cl without /MP, only to run tests/luajit/test_*.c (1 file). test_lua.cmd:58-59 instead links engine-ci\_build (or the stale engine\_build) lua51.lib, built by MSBuild and possibly older than the sources. Slice tests use a third choice (finding above).
kept.fix: test_luajit.cmd builds lua51_test.lib only when a stamp of the luajit-2/src sources changes (the same stamp approach as runlua) and with /MP. test_lua.cmd, test_trader_identity_api and the pelican/trader native helpers link that lib. Then there is one LuaJIT, always the current sources, and no dependency on engine-ci/_build existing.

kept.title: With COOP_TEST_OUT set, the LuaJIT lib packs all coop test objects of build_tests.cmd
kept.detail: Both build_tests.cmd (:37, objects in %OUT%\obj) and test_luajit.cmd (:14, objects in %OUT%\obj) use %COOP_TEST_OUT% as OUT. run_all_tests.cmd runs build_tests and then test_luajit in the same environment, so `lib /out:lua51_test.lib *.obj` (:48) also archives about 190 test_*.obj/coop_*.obj. COOP_TEST_OUT is exactly what parallel agents are told to set (build_tests.cmd:4). Without the variable the folders differ (temp\tests vs temp\tests_luajit), which is why this has stayed hidden.
kept.fix: test_luajit.cmd uses %OUT%\luajit\obj (its own subfolder) and lists the LuaJIT objects explicitly instead of *.obj.

kept.title: Six different scratch-folder patterns: shared fixed folders collide in parallel runs, uuid folders leak
kept.detail: conftest `work` (:20-25) cleans up, but most slice tests bypass it. Fixed shared folders: test_silencer_detach.py:12/:37 temp/silencer_detach; _work() in container_reject:41, items_gift_late, local_zone_release, move_admission_wiring, texture_descr_slice, which is temp/<name> unless COOP_TEST_OUT is set; trade_delivery.py:15. Two agents running pytest overwrite each other's compile.cmd/.exe (LNK1104 or a wrong exe). Never cleaned up: client_ammo_reload.py:73 (temp/client_ammo_reload: 77 leftover folders counted), trader_identity_api.py:24 (52), clone_pending_fire.py:17, clone_placement_hooks.py:15 and weapon_clone_wgl.py:29 under a dated temp/clone-placement-2026-11-09 (hooks 63, pending-fire 51, wgl 81). test_ci_sync.py:32/:67 uses unittest + TemporaryDirectory, which fails on read-only git objects on Windows: 15 temp/ci-sync-* folders left over. test_release/test_stand_patterns use pytest's tmp_path on C:.
kept.fix: Add one module-scoped `native_work` fixture to conftest, a unique folder under temp/pytest_tools removed with onexc=_force as `work` does, and use it everywhere. Convert test_ci_sync.py to pytest functions on `work`. Delete the leaked folders once.
kept.correction: The conftest is tests/tools/conftest.py (work at :19-25); tests/conftest.py does not exist. The cited patterns are confirmed: silencer_detach :12/:37 use a fixed temp/silencer_detach; container_reject :41-44 and trade_delivery :14-16 use temp/<name> unless COOP_TEST_OUT is set. Leftover counts: client_ammo_reload 82, trader_identity 52, clone-placement hooks 63, pending-fire 51, wgl 81. The stated cause of the 15 temp/ci-sync-* leftovers is wrong. tempfile.TemporaryDirectory._rmtree already resets permissions and retries on PermissionError, so read-only git objects do not explain them. All 15 date from 23.11 16:31-16:36, which suggests interrupted runs or files held open. The rest of the fix (one module-scoped native_work fixture) stands.

kept.title: C++ definition extractor copied 4 times with 2 signatures; 13 test modules import it from other test modules
kept.detail: definition(source, signature) is in test_campfire_damage.py:13 and test_client_ammo_reload.py:14. definition(path, signature) is in test_weapon_brief_info.py:13 and test_weapon_clone_wgl.py:13. Other shapes: tests/test_s6_hub_paths.py:19, test_s6_npc_paths.py:22, test_story_worldstate.py:21, test_survival_s6_paths.py:26. 13 files do `from test_weapon_brief_info import ROOT, definition` (or from test_client_ammo_reload / test_weapon_clone_wgl), so the gate's move-admission test depends on importing another test module. ROOT already lives in conftest. The token regex handles // /* */ and "strings" but not char literals ('{' '}' or '"'), so a sliced function containing one would be cut at the wrong brace.
kept.fix: tests/tools/native_slice.py with definition(text_or_path, signature) and declaration(); handle char literals in the token regex; import ROOT from conftest. Drop the copies.

kept.title: Lua tests read GAMMA scripts from a moving or missing place, so results depend on the last stand deploy
kept.detail: test_lua.cmd:52 defaults GAMMA_SCRIPTS to E:\RayLinkGames\GAMMA\game-dev\gamedata\scripts. That is the stand, whose gamedata stand_head.py deploy and stand_overlay.py rewrite with our Core and GAMMA layers on every stand run. Fallbacks point at stands that are gone (Test-Path false for both): tests/lua/support/mod_source.lua:16-19 uses E:\AnomalyCoopGamma, then untracked temp/review/corpus/merged; test_trader_supplies.lua:136, test_weapon_transform_sources.lua:7, test_pelican_weapon_jam.lua:6 and support/trader_catalog.py:15 use E:/RayLink2/gamma. tests/tools/test_gamma_minimap.py:17 compares with E:\RayLink2\... behind `if GAMMA_16.exists()` (:73), so that check silently never runs. kept.correction: Confirmed, except that the GAMMA_16 guard is at test_gamma_minimap.py:80, not :73. Paths: test_lua.cmd:52 defaults to the game-dev stand, which exists and is rewritten by every stand deploy. mod_source.lua:16-19 uses E:\AnomalyCoopGamma, then temp/review/corpus/merged. test_trader_supplies.lua:136, test_weapon_transform_sources.lua:7, test_pelican_weapon_jam.lua:6 and trader_catalog.py:15 use E:/RayLink2/..., and Test-Path is False for E:\RayLink2 and E:\AnomalyCoopGamma. kept.title: One Lua test scans the whole stock and stand config trees through Python on every run (about 70 s)
kept.detail: test_trader_rep_modes.lua:10 runs os.execute("python -B tests/lua/support/trader_catalog.py"), which builds Game(folder).configs() for ../anomaly-ref/unpacked and for the whole GAMMA tree (trader_catalog.py:15-30) on every run. Gaps between consecutive files' timestamps in temp/lua/out (23.11 16:29:58-16:35:16, 720 rows in 317 s) show about 70 s for trader_rep_modes and about 66 s for allies. The cause for allies is not established, and rows from overlapping runs may share the default out folder. test_trader_reputation.lua:352 shells out to python too.
kept.fix: Generate the trader catalog once per GAMMA snapshot (cache the JSON under temp keyed by the snapshot fingerprint, or commit it as a fixture regenerated by a tool) and have the test read it. Profile test_allies separately.
kept.correction: The scan runs twice per suite, not once: test_trader_rep_modes.lua:10 and test_trader_supplies.lua:4 both run trader_catalog.py. Both write and then read the fixed temp/trader_reputation/catalog.lua and coverage.json. The '70 s every run' cost is not established. In the same 23.11 run, the trader_supplies row came 5 s after trader_reputation, so a warm scan takes at most 5 s. The 70 s before trader_rep_modes (16:33:46 to 16:34:56) is most likely the first, cold pass over the GAMMA and anomaly-ref trees, or rows from overlapping runs. The cause of the 67 s gap before allies is unknown. The fix (cache the catalog keyed by a snapshot fingerprint, generated once) still removes one scan and the shared fixed path. Payoff low to medium.

kept.title: Lua driver runs about 720 test processes strictly one after another through cmd
kept.detail: run_all.lua:108 os.execute per file, and per answer set for the 4 SETS of Core files (:79), sequentially; about 317 s per run (temp/lua/out timestamps). Each test is its own process with its own state, so the runs are independent and could be parallel.
kept.fix: Run N at a time: a small Python driver with concurrent.futures, or batches started with `start /b` and waited on a marker. Keep the same judge() rules and the per-file out files.
kept.correction: Running sequentially is confirmed (run_all.lua:105-110). But the claim 'each test is its own process, so runs are independent' is wrong. Several tests write fixed paths: test_trader_rep_modes and test_trader_supplies both regenerate and read temp/trader_reputation/catalog.lua; test_hud_revive.lua:266 and test_hud_v2.lua:482 write temp/lua/<fixed>; test_menu_char.lua:903 writes temp/menu_char_gamma_starts.ltx; trader_reputation writes temp/trader_reputation/native-goodwill.lua. A Core file also runs 4 times, once per answer set (@hostplay/@srv_world/@srv_map/@none), and those runs would share any fixed path. Each test first needs a per-run scratch folder (for example from an env var the driver sets) before N-way parallelism is safe. Risk medium, not low. Behaviour change stays false.

kept.title: engine-ci is a hand-patched copy (allow-list of folders, skipped vcxproj, a gap finder) instead of a checkout
kept.detail: SKIP (:26-29) still excludes xrGame.vcxproj(.filters) 'all work packages landed (2026-10-20 17:59)'. New coop files are added to the CI project through vcxproj_add.py (:161). SOURCE_DIRS (:40-44) is an allow-list, and ci_gap.py exists to find what it misses. changed_files (:85-91) reads every file of those folders in both trees on each run. engine-ci is already a git worktree (its HEAD is 0e41d67a of 2026-11-21 with files copied over), and its xrGame.vcxproj differs from main (SHA1 F4F005E6 vs 3A805C5D; the 1304 ClCompile items match today). A non-coop file added to the main project will not reach CI (the 'b40.3' trap of DEBUG_DESIGN.md:671).
kept.fix: For --committed: `git -C engine-ci checkout --detach <engine HEAD>` (or `git worktree add`) and then write raylink_build.h. That drops SKIP, SOURCE_DIRS, the vcxproj_add call and ci_gap.py. Keep the working-tree mode only if it is still needed.

kept.title: ci_gap.py copies ci_sync's folder list and has drifted from it
kept.detail: ci_gap DIRS (:6) = xrGame, xrCoop, xrEngine, xrServerEntities, xrCore, Layers, xrSound. ci_sync SOURCE_DIRS (:40-44) also has 'src/3rd party/luabind' and 'src/3rd party/luajit-2/src'. So ci_gap reports those two folders as gaps that are not there. It also runs one `git show` process per tracked file outside DIRS (:13).
kept.fix: Import ci_sync.SOURCE_DIRS (or make it `ci_sync.py --gaps`) and read blobs with one `git cat-file --batch`. It goes away entirely with the checkout-based ci_sync.
kept.correction: The drift is real: ci_gap DIRS (:6) lacks 'src/3rd party/luabind' and 'src/3rd party/luajit-2/src' from ci_sync SOURCE_DIRS (:40-44). But ci_gap reports a file only when its HEAD blob differs from the engine-ci copy (:17-21). So luabind and LuaJIT files show up as gaps only when ci_sync has not copied them yet; after a sync they are not reported. The concrete cost is one `git show` process (:14) for each of the many luabind and LuaJIT files on every run, plus false 'gaps' before a sync. This is drift, not a wrong report after a sync. Kind: duplicate or structure, not bug. Payoff low.

kept.title: Test names and headers record history (review ids, task codes, temp paths) instead of what is tested
kept.detail: Native files named by task code: test_mode_review_e1, test_srv_ops_done_e1, test_item_lines_o7, test_issue_p45_kill_record, test_initial_set_e2, test_srv_tails_o6, test_protocol_f3/f3a/f5, test_mode_s6_answers, test_s6_integration, test_s6_npc, test_story_s6, test_survival_s6. Their headers cite temp/w9rev/A-REV-E-1.md, temp/r30/design/R32-final.md, 'report RL-89RT-DQYR #1664' and 'Before: ...'. 37 TEST() names carry codes such as _S6/_F3/_E1. Python: 10 tests named test_review3_*/test_review5_b3_*/test_review5_b4_*. check_layers.py has 46 review markers and test_gates.py 34. Runner comments carry dates: test_lua.cmd:10, :50, build_tests.cmd:36, run_all_tests.cmd:12 'review 4, B5'.
